verdicts.reason: The need is real, but the proposed mechanism fails on three independent atoms. (1) OWNER: it registers dialog paths 'into the same FsBroker retained-scope set', but FsBroker never decides Allow. FsBroker::read/write call dispatch_privileged, which calls evaluate(manifest,...) and lends a ScopePermit whose grant_index selects the retained grant; 'Only the guard can mint a permit' and it names a manifest grant. A dialog path absent from the manifest is denied by evaluate before the broker runs. So the mint is either a keld-guard API/permission-model change (not named, and in tension with the approved KEL-102 'immutable-host-session-snapshot' model and D9 'no manifest-schema change') or a second policy owner in keld-native (forbidden by KEL-102-D5 and the spec's Reuse rule). The stated unknown ('re-preparation cost') misclassifies an ownership question as a performance one. (2) ORACLE: the sibling pattern `<name>.*` (prototype: `file.bkp`) does not match draw.io. Its drafts and backups are prefix-named in the same directory: `.$<basename><unique>.dtmp`, `.$<basename>.bkp`, plus legacy `~$` forms. (3) LIFECYCLE: 'never persisted' and 'dialog only' contradict the same oracle. draw.io persists blessedPaths (cap 500) so Open Recent works after restart, and it also blesses paths from file association (open-file) and command-line argv. Separately, the first proof runs under LegacySandboxOff where Bun has ambient fs, so this decision is not needed for that milestone.

verdicts.reason: The direction (host-minted dynamic grants flowing into the FsBroker scope set; arch 05 dialog row 'scoped-path grants flow into fs scopes') stands, and the Electron return shapes are correct. But the specific mint shape is contradicted by the very drawio oracle the decision cites, on four points. (1) 'open -> fs.read leaf' is wrong: drawio blesses every open-dialog path and its write gate accepts any blessed path, so File>Open then Save writes back to the opened path with no save dialog. A read-only open grant fails F06-T2's own acceptance criterion 'draw.io open -> edit -> save completes'. (2) The sibling pattern '<name>.*' matches none of drawio's siblings: they are prefix-named ('.$' + basename + optional counter + '.dtmp', '.$' + basename + '.bkp', legacy '~$' prefix) and matched by startsWith. The trap's test oracle 'write <path>.bkp' is therefore also wrong. (3) 'revoked on generation death and never persisted' breaks Open Recent: drawio persists its blessed set (cap 500) in electron-store specifically so Open Recent works across launches, and it also blesses paths that never came from a dialog (argv, second-instance, macOS open-file). (4) Leaf grants do not cover Zettlr's directory picks (openDirectory + createDirectory), which need subtree read+write and are persisted as workspace roots. Sequencing: the first proof runs drawio under the explicit legacy profile (ambient fs), so D1 is not on the first-proof path and should be parked as a decision ticket, not designed in detail now.

verdicts.reason: Host ownership of UI handles, host-to-Bun click dispatch with (commandId, focused window, KeyboardEvent), one shared accelerator parser, and host-side role execution all match Electron's own structure: one StringToAccelerator used by menu and globalShortcut; on macOS role items are wired to native selectors; click receives (event, focusedWindow, focusedWebContents). The doc quotes are exact. Four corrections do not overturn it. (1) The 'unknown' popup ordering is determinable from source for macOS: menu-will-close fires first, then the item click, then the popup callback (the close callback is deliberately posted async 'so that itemSelected runs before the close callback'). Zettlr's comment says the same. The F06 trap oracle 'click then will-close then callback' is wrong. (2) 'Electron ignores click when role is set' is the doc sentence, but the implementation falls back to the user click when role execution returns false (macOS-native roles in JS, or a window/webContents role with nothing focused), and quit/close roles run app.quit()/window.close(), which emit vetoable events - so 'without a round trip' is false for those two. (3) Item properties (checked, enabled, label, menu.items) are synchronous getters and the checkbox flip happens in JS on click, so Bun must hold the authoritative item state with the host as projection; the rejected alternative (a) 'two sources of truth' is partly unavoidable and the ticket should say which side is authoritative. (4) The default menu is a JS Menu built from five role items at will-finish-launching and is visible through Menu.getApplicationMenu(); building it 'host-side' only would make getApplicationMenu() return null where Electron returns a Menu - build it in the facade through the normal setApplicationMenu path and delete the special case. Sizing: first-proof demand is the application menu only (drawio: buildFromTemplate + setApplicationMenu with role items and a few click items; setApplicationMenu(null) off-mac). Tray, Notification and popup have Zettlr-only demand (one site each family); globalShortcut and powerSaveBlocker have zero resolved call sites. Split D2 so only the application-menu slice is on the first-proof path.

verdicts.reason: What survives: the v44.4.5 W3C clipboard shape as baseline (drawio's one clipboard path uses exactly it), a single host call per write for atomicity, and the 16 MiB / 8 MiB ceilings as real constants. Four sub-claims are contradicted by primary sources. (1) NativeImage is not immutable: setTemplateImage, addRepresentation and the writable isMacTemplateImage property mutate it. (2) createFromPath is not 'one FsBroker fs.read': it returns synchronously and, for a name without a DPI suffix, reads the base file plus eleven suffixed siblings (@2x, @3x, @1x, @4x, ...), through an asar-aware reader. (3) createFromDataURL(png).toPNG() is not a byte pass-through in Electron: the PNG is decoded into a Skia representation and toPNG re-encodes, so ancillary chunks are dropped and an invalid payload yields an empty image and an empty buffer. F06-T1's criterion 'toPNG() byte equality for PNG input' is therefore not a valid oracle in either direction. (4) The sync mechanism is misattributed and unavailable: Linear KEL-127 is the program issue 'post-audit convergence and Mac no-Rust product proof' and contains no blocking-CALL primitive; the 'blocking CALL with a deadline, rate-limited, dev-warned' rule is arch 02 text about renderer sendSync. The map's resolved fact is that the Bun kipc client cannot block, so 'Zettlr is runnable with a config-only change' is false until the worker-owned transport exists. The same gap covers NativeImage's synchronous transforms that Zettlr uses (resize, toJPEG(100), toDataURL, getAspectRatio), which D5 leaves host-side. Demand and sizing: Zettlr's resolved legacy clipboard demand is two call sites (one synchronous readText, one fire-and-forget writeImage); readImage, writeText and availableFormats have zero call sites, and Zettlr is the second corpus, so the quirk flag is not first-proof work. Also unevaluated: Bun 1.4.2 ships a built-in Bun.Image codec (system backend), which makes rejected alternative (b) 'pure-TS decode' a strawman - though it is Promise-only, so it does not by itself satisfy the sync contract.

verdicts.correction: Restate D5 as: (a) NativeImage is a Bun-side mutable value (template flag, representation list) with no host handle; (b) createFromPath is a synchronous multi-file probe (base + DPI siblings) - served by ambient fs under the legacy profile for the first proof, and under strict it needs either a scope that covers the suffixed siblings plus a blocking read or an explicit scaffolded gap; (c) replace the T1 byte-equality oracle with 'output decodes to the same dimensions and pixels as the input' plus a negative control 'invalid PNG data URL -> isEmpty() true and toPNG().length === 0', and record pass-through as a declared divergence because it retains ancillary chunks Electron strips; (d) cite arch 02 (not KEL-127) for the blocking-CALL rule and state that every synchronous Bun-main member (legacy clipboard.readText, NativeImage resize/toJPEG/toDataURL on non-pass-through input) is SCAFFOLDED behind the PANEL-P1 worker-owned transport decision, or reopen the Bun-side codec alternative with Bun.Image named as the existing facility and its Promise-only shape as the blocker; (e) shrink the quirk to the two demanded members (sync readText, writeImage), note writeImage needs no blocking call, and park the whole quirk until Zettlr is the active corpus; (f) first-proof scope is exactly drawio's writeText/readText/write([ClipboardItem]) with PNG pass-through.

Two corrections. (1) The 'declared divergence' on Linux basic_text is mis-scored. In v44.4.5 source, with the basic_text backend isEncryptionAvailable() is false and encryptString throws 'Encryption is not available' by default; plaintext only happens after the app opts in with setUsePlainTextEncryption(true). Keld's fail-closed behaviour therefore matches Electron's default, and the only divergence is refusing that opt-in. The F06 trap oracle 'Electron oracle returns basic_text + encrypts' is wrong for the default path. (2) The answer does not separate the two API generations: encryptString/decryptString/isEncryptionAvailable are synchronous and 'host performs encrypt/decrypt' cannot serve them while the Bun client cannot block; the v44.4.5 doc recommends the async API and says the sync one may be deprecated. extra_findings.finding: Unhandled-rejection divergence affects every F06 denial path and is on the first-proof path. Electron's main process survives an uncaught error (shows an error box and continues); a stock Bun process exits 1 on an unhandled promise rejection. drawio drops the promise at all three shell.openExternal sites, so any facade rejection there (user decline under D4, manifest denial, OS failure) would kill the main role. No equivalent handler exists in the @keld/electron source. This is a lifecycle-unit concern discovered here, not an F06 design item: route it to the lifecycle/bootstrap epic as its own conformance cell.

verdicts.reason: The proposed single resolver owner does not work on the pinned Bun. FACT (executed, Bun 1.4.2 macOS arm64): a plugin registered through bunfig `preload` with onResolve filter /.*/ is called for the entry file and for relative specifiers, but never for bare `electron`, never for `electron/main|renderer|common|utility`, and never for `child_process`/`node:child_process`. This held for static ESM import (.mjs and .ts), dynamic import, CJS require, and a require inside a node_modules dependency. With a real `electron` in node_modules the app got the real package; with none, Bun auto-resolved `electron` to ~/.bun/install/cache/electron@44.5.1 and subpaths failed with 'Cannot find package'. The same onResolve does fire for bare specifiers inside Bun.build, so only the bundler half of the claim holds, and arch 06 section 2 says `keld build` uses the app's own bundler, so Keld owns no Bun.build call to attach it to. Second refuted sub-claim: 'tsconfig paths stays the editor/type mapping'. FACT: on Bun 1.4.2 tsconfig paths is a live runtime resolver that outranks node_modules for bare `electron`, in app code and in a node_modules CJS dependency, while subpaths still go to node_modules; Node ignores it. Keeping it beside any other alias gives two runtime owners and can load two module instances. Third: the decision duplicates X02-A1, which the published plan already names as the one alias owner. The alternative A2 never evaluated passes: a package.json dependency whose key is `electron` plus an exports map resolved all five specifiers for import and require, in app code and in a CJS dependency, on both Bun 1.4.2 and Node 26.10. That is also what arch 04 section 2 already says ('@keld/* deps replace electron*').

verdicts.reason: The delivery mechanism survives; the value contract as written does not. SURVIVES (FACT): host-minted facts readable synchronously are demanded at module evaluation by the first-proof app: draw.io constructs electron-store at top level, electron-store 11.0.2 reads app.getPath('userData') and app.getVersion() in that path, and electron-is-dev 3.0.1 (pulled in by electron-context-menu 5.1.0, imported by draw.io) reads electron.app.isPackaged at its own module evaluation. process.md quotes for defaultApp/mas/windowsStore/sandboxed/contextIsolated are accurate at v44.4.5. REFUTED clause 1 (FACT): 'defaultApp left undefined' without a host-minted argv breaks draw.io. draw.io does `if (process.defaultApp != true) argv.unshift(null)` then parses `argv.slice(2)`; process.md defines defaultApp as true exactly when the app path occupies an argv slot ('useful to determine how many arguments will need to be sliced off from process.argv'). A Bun role is spawned as runtime + script + args (INFERENCE from role spawn passing configured args; not measured in a draw.io run), so undefined defaultApp makes the main script path the first positional token, i.e. a file to open/export. REFUTED clause 2 (FACT): 'read synchronously by @keld/electron at import' is too late for process.type. verdicts.reason: The mirror choice itself survives (host-authoritative, generation-stamped, synchronous reads; the Bun client cannot block, so it is the only candidate). Three stated rules are contradicted by pinned primary evidence and must change before ticket text is cut. (1) Write-through ('the facade applies the requested value to the mirror') is wrong on the first-proof OS: the pinned doc says a macOS setBounds with y:20 reads back y:38, and that isFullScreen() must not be trusted until enter/leave-full-screen has fired; the macOS source clamps to min/max size, ignores setBounds while fullscreen, and reports fullscreen from the style mask only after the asynchronous transition. An optimistic mirror would report true where Electron reports false; draw.io does win.setFullScreen(!win.isFullScreen()) and setFullScreen(true) straight after construction. (2) isMaximized is not an event flag: on macOS it is derived from the frame (isZoomed, forced false while minimized or fullscreen), so a mirror driven by maximize/unmaximize events diverges; Zettlr reads getBounds() and isMaximized() together inside its resize/move/maximize callback. (3) 'Zero allocation per read' is false for getBounds/getSize/getPosition: Electron returns a fresh Rectangle/array per call, and a shared object would let caller mutation corrupt the mirror. Corpus numbers are also partly token-scan artifacts: Zettlr has 0 BrowserWindow.getSize sites (all 3 are nativeImage.getSize) and 1 BrowserWindow 'resize' listener, not 7; draw.io has 5 window isDestroyed guards plus 1 webContents.isDestroyed, and two of them are in progress-bar.js, not electron.js.

When querying for a BrowserWindow's fullscreen status, you should ensure that either the enter-full-screen or leave-full-screen events have been emitted'; maximize 'will also show (but not focus) the window if it isn't being displayed already'. FACT shell/browser/native_window_mac.mm v44.4.5: IsMaximized (L605-619) returns false if minimized/fullscreen, else [window_ isZoomed] or a frame comparison; IsFullscreen (L726) = HasStyleMask(NSWindowStyleMaskFullScreen); SetFullScreen (L691-724) queues pending transitions; SetBounds (L730-750) returns early in fullscreen and clamps to min/max. verdicts.correction: Keep the mirror, change the rules. (a) Each host event carries one complete per-window snapshot (bounds, content bounds, isMaximized, isMinimized, isFullScreen, isVisible, isFocused, destroyed) computed by the host at one instant and stamped with the generation; the facade never derives isMaximized from maximize/unmaximize events. (b) Setters do not write the requested value into the mirror. Classify each setter from an oracle fixture: for setFullScreen (asynchronous in Electron on macOS) the mirror changes only on the host snapshot, which matches Electron; for setBounds/setSize/setPosition either wait for the host snapshot and publish the read-your-write lag as a divergence, or apply the documented clamps locally. One conformance entry per setter records the setter->getter sequence on macOS first. (c) Object-returning getters return a fresh copy per call; the zero-allocation claim applies to boolean getters only. (d) Add two ordering atoms: window-state events and renderer-originated IPC share the one ordered app link, so getFocusedWindow() is current when a renderer message arrives (draw.io windowAction/toggleFullscreen depend on it); and the mirror is updated before the Electron-visible event is emitted. (e) Record the tombstone as resolved fact, not unknown. (f) Correct the demand line: Zettlr getSize 0, window 'resize' listeners 1; draw.io 5 window isDestroyed + 1 webContents.isDestroyed.

verdicts.reason: The Electron quotes, the 'ipc-message-sync' event and the six Zettlr sites (preload/index.ts:37,57,63,74; pinia/config.ts:28,49; draw.io 0) all check out, and the per-engine cell with an explicit async-only divergence matches the map's resolved position. The question as posed is still unanswered for the engine that matters: no evidence exists that a renderer can block on WKWebView, and Zettlr on macOS is the first corpus app that needs it. It is not needed for the first proof (draw.io has 0 sendSync). Separately, four parts of the proposed contract are wrong or underspecified. (1) 'A CALL on the same guarded channel as invoke' misstates dispatch: a sync message goes to on-listeners (WebFrameMain.ipc, then webContents.ipc, then ipcMain) plus the webContents 'ipc-message-sync' event, never to handle() handlers. verdicts.reason: The per-engine isolation honesty (WebKit real, WebView2 emulated) is not contradicted, but the macOS check mark is. The decision says exposeInMainWorld is 'installed by the pageWorld facade pattern already used for window.keld'. FACT: that pattern is a window.postMessage relay between the two worlds - asynchronous, structured-clone only, one pending call. FACT: Electron defines contextBridge as 'a safe, bi-directional, synchronous bridge' in which functions are proxied in both directions and return values, Promises, Elements and Blobs cross. The existing pattern cannot carry any of the shapes the corpus needs: (1) draw.io exposes window.electron and window.process and the page must see them before its first script runs - a posted message task gives no such ordering; (2) draw.io's request(msg, callback, error) passes page functions into the isolated world, including a function nested inside an object argument (msg.listener for watchFile) that is called repeatedly; functions are not structured-cloneable; (3) Zettlr needs synchronous returns across the bridge (window.config.get 36 sites, config.set 20, getPathForFile 3), a function returned from a bridged function (ipc.on returns stopListening; getCitationCallback 8 sites returns a function), and a File object passed page-to-isolated. INFERENCE: a synchronous cross-world trampoline is plausible on WebKit (DOM event dispatch is synchronous across worlds) but that is a new mechanism with no evidence yet, and it is the first-proof critical path. Sequencing defect: blocked_by names only the WebView2 prototype (Windows, not first proof) and KEL-79; the macOS contextBridge experiment exists only as an unlinked prototype candidate.

INFERENCE: it is viable as a transport (strings only, callable from page code too, so the document nonce must still gate it); that needs the same prototype. (2) Therefore the fall-through rule 'if sync XHR is blocked, sendSync becomes a documented failure' is premature. (3) 'response body is the SCV-encoded returnValue' cannot be read as binary: the XHR standard throws InvalidAccessError when responseType or timeout is set on a synchronous request in a Window, so the reply must be text-safe and the deadline can only be host-side. Also unspecified versus Electron: Electron has no deadline - sendSync with no listener only warns in main and the renderer stays blocked - so deadline expiry and rate-limit behaviour are Keld divergences that need defined outcomes (a rate limit that throws would break Zettlr's high-frequency config.get).

verdicts.reason: The core choice (host-owned child webview rather than iframe; Tier 3; not on any corpus path - zero <webview> call sites in all three apps) survives and stays parked. The attribute mapping as written is wrong in three places. (1) Partition: Electron has three cases, not two - 'persist:' prefix is a persistent session shared by every page with the same partition; no prefix is an in-memory session, also shared by name; unset uses the app's default session. 'persist: = identity-bound, else memory-only' sends the unset case (the common one) to a memory-only store and loses sharing by name. (2) The cited owner fact is a misread: KEL-135 gives one store per app identity supplied to every view, not one per view; a partition dimension contradicts that spec's current invariant and needs a KEL-135 spec change, not consumption. (3) 'nodeintegration ... refused at attach with a code' diverges from Electron: security-critical preferences are inherited from the embedder and the attribute is ignored, and the guest still attaches; refusing would fail guests Electron loads. The mapping also omits httpreferrer, webpreferences and nodeintegrationinsubframes, and the answer text omits that most <webview> methods are synchronous for the caller.
verdicts.evidence: Electron v44.4.5 docs/api/webview-tag.md: partition ('If the partition is unset then default session of the app will be used'; 'By assigning the same partition, multiple pages can share the same session'; 'can only be modified before the first navigation'), webpreferences ('the guest inherits that value and the corresponding webpreferences entry is ignored'), 'Most methods called on the webview from the host page require a synchronous call to the main process', 'Popups are disabled by default', getWebContentsId 'Returns number'; lib/browser/guest-view-manager.ts makeWebPreferences inheritedWebPreferences loop and 'if (event.defaultPrevented) return -1' - retrieved 2026-10-06. Linear KEL-135 In Progress (fetched 2026-10-06), acceptance scoped to per-app identity. corpus: grep -i webview => only webviewTag:false and the preventDefault handler in draw.io.
verdicts.correction: Keep the decision parked with only the direction recorded. When it is opened: map unset partition to the embedder app's default store, a non-prefixed name to a named in-memory store shared by all views using that name, 'persist:name' to a named persistent store shared likewise, and raise the multi-store requirement against the KEL-135 spec as a change. Changing the emission point silently changes what the replayed Ready means in generation ≥2 (a window exists) and makes the adoption shim dead or wrong; F01-T2's AC1/AC3 already contradict each other on this.

hidden_coupling.coupling: At least four 'generation' notions are used interchangeably: Bun role generation (tombstones, stale-generation errors in F02-T2), WindowGeneration (F02-T2), bridge navigation_generation u64 rotated on navigation start (keld-wv macos_bridge.rs:335), guard Principal::Webview.generation (0 in live backends per the refuter), plus X05's 'per-window state generation' for the mirror. hidden_coupling.fix: F04-A4's resolution names each generation, its minting owner and rotation point; add edge F04-T3 ← F04-A4; forbid the bare word 'generation' in ticket ACs.

hidden_coupling.coupling: The world decision silently changes three other atoms: what executeJavaScriptInIsolatedWorld's worldId can address, where F03-T2's 'same-document change via the isolated-world reporter' runs, and which world host-initiated executeJavaScript lands in (must never be the KEL-142 trusted world holding handler and nonce).
hidden_coupling.fix: Drop executeJavaScriptInIsolatedWorld from F03-T5 (zero demand); add an AC to F03-T5 'app-supplied script never executes in the trusted bridge world' and an edge F03-T2 ← PANEL-D21 for the reporter placement.

hidden_coupling.coupling: Channel grants ↔ migrate. The runtime boundary (enumerated el:<channel>) is only as good as the list migrate emits; F04-T3 carries a migrate AC ('el:* is refused by migrate'), X02-T3 seeds windows.<w>.channels which the guard parses and ignores today, and the list for draw.io is derivable from main-side ipcMain registrations (25 literals) but not from the preload, which forwards page-chosen names.

hidden_coupling.coupling: Page URL identity. draw.io authorizes every IPC with senderFrame.url.startsWith(codeUrl) (:694-700) and filters file:// loads by the same prefix (:1010-1022). If the host serves the app from any origin other than file://<codeDir> (F07-A6 contemplates replacing file:// origins; WebView2 'virtual host mapping' in F05-T4), validateSender returns false for all 25 channels and the app is silently dead.
hidden_coupling.fix: AC in F05-T4: the document URL reported to the app (webContents.getURL, senderFrame.url) equals the file:// URL the app loaded; edge F04-T3 ← F05-T4; F07-A6 records this as a constraint.

hidden_coupling.coupling: F06-T4 executes menu `role` items host-side 'without a round trip'. draw.io's menu has role 'close' (:2047) and role 'quit' (:2042); executed natively they would bypass the cancelable close/quit protocol that F02-T3/F01-T3 exist to provide.

hidden_coupling.coupling: Host-pushed mirrors (window bounds/focus, displays, theme) write events toward a role that may be parked in a sync dialog; the link stalls at 8 KiB (measured probe). Mirror event volume ('move'/'resize') therefore changes whether the blocking transport is safe, and a parked role reads stale mirror values on wake.
hidden_coupling.fix: PANEL-P1 arm B adds a mirror-event flood during the park; F02-T2 states the staleness contract (ordered replay before the sync call returns).

hidden_coupling.coupling: Updater disablement depends on an environment variable: PANEL-D14 has migrate write DRAWIO_DISABLE_UPDATE=true into 'the host-declared role environment', read at module top level (:75). hidden_coupling.coupling: F01-T5 AC3 makes requestSingleInstanceLock() without a config declaration a typed diagnostic; draw.io quits when the call returns false (:1718-1722). Whether the proof app boots therefore depends on migrate emitting the declaration, which is listed in X02-T3 but not edged.

Role: Prototype evidence for one question. You do not design the transport, write a spec, or touch product code.

Goal: Decide with measurements whether a single kipc link owned by a Bun Worker for the whole session lets the Bun main thread park without stalling the link, and still deliver a sync REPLY and replay EVENTs in order.

Success criteria:
- Arm A (control, socket on main thread): under a 10 s Atomics.wait park, with the peer writing 100 x 64-byte EVENT frames per second, record bytes accepted before the writer stalls (expected 8192) and the Rust host writer's exact error and elapsed time (expected KELD-IPC-006 near the 5 s APP_LINK_IO_DEADLINE). State which entry point drove the Rust writer; if none exposes the write deadline publicly, report that instead of copying code.
- Arm B (socket in a Worker, SharedArrayBuffer ring, Atomics.notify): same load plus one 10,000-EVENT burst. Pass = every byte accepted, no writer timeout, a sync CALL issued before the park returns its REPLY value while parked, and all 10,000 EVENTs reach main-thread listeners in sequence order with zero drops or duplicates.
- Arm E: the host closes the link (or retires the generation) mid-park. Pass = main wakes with a typed error inside the deadline and no 'closed' event is fabricated.
- Report the ring/buffer bound you used, the EVENT bytes buffered during the park, and what happens at overflow.
- Sync round-trip p50/p99 over 1,000 calls is recorded as a diagnostic only, never as a claim.
- Every frame is a real @keld/kipc frame; one link only. A second socket for the role is a fail, not a design.

packets.decision: On macOS the app preload and the renderer compat runtime run in a content world separate from the KEL-142 bridge world, with their own world-scoped message handler, rather than sharing the bridge world.
facts: FACT (measured, world-probe run by this agent 2026-10-06, macOS 26.5.1, system WKWebView; source and output in scratchpad/prototypes/world-probe): a script placed in the same content world as a bridge-shaped script read the world-scoped handler object directly, posted a forged message that reached the native handler from the main frame, wrapped the global bind hook, captured the host-delivered document nonce, posted a forged invoke carrying the correct nonce, leaked the nonce to the page, and relayed page-chosen bytes to the raw native handler.
FACT (measured, same run): the same script placed in a named content world saw the handler as undefined and the bind hook as undefined, and no forged message reached the native handler.

FACT (measured, same run): a hardened bridge script could freeze its bind hook (the nonce then did not leak), but its attempt to shadow window.webkit threw 'Attempting to change value of a readonly property', so the handler stayed reachable and both forged messages still arrived.
FACT (measured, same run): window.postMessage crosses content worlds, and the handler also exists in subframes of the same world (those messages arrive with isMainFrame false).

FACT: Apple documents that the user content controller defines the handler function 'in all frames in the specified content world' (developer.apple.com, WKUserContentController addScriptMessageHandler(_:contentWorld:name:), JSON endpoint fetched 2026-10-06).

FACT: the live bridge registers its handler in the default client world, assigns the bind and result hooks as plain writable globals, and calls JSON.stringify, Number.isInteger, Array.isArray and Array.from at call time rather than capturing them; the host rejects non-main-frame messages and stale or forged nonces (crates/keld-wv/src/wkwebview/macos_bridge.rs at b4b907c3, read 2026-10-06).

FACT: KEL-142 section 5.1 says the page world must not be able to access the native message-handler object, its handler name, or the host's document binding, and that a page-callable relay 'must accept no broader shape than window.keld.invoke'; AC2 requires the nonce to be absent from page globals and request arguments, and 'Deleting content-world isolation ... must fail a named test' (docs/specs/kel142-macos-renderer-bridge-api.md, read 2026-10-06).

FACT: draw.io's preload calls contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld twice and exposes sendMessage(action, args), which forwards a page-chosen channel to ipcRenderer.send (corpus drawio-desktop @2edf9fb, src/main/electron-preload.js).
FACT: F07-T1 (GitHub #484) lists PANEL-D21 in blocked_by and names a 'KEL-142 spec revision (third world/relay)' as an external predecessor (publish_plan.json).
FACT (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06): KEL-142 Done (completed 2026-10-01), parent KEL-139 Done; KEL-79 Backlog, unassigned. No open Linear issue owns a KEL-142 revision.
inferences: INFERENCE: the world-probe mimics the bridge's two decisive properties (world-scoped handler, writable global bind hook) rather than running the real bridge. The real bridge has the same two properties in code, so the same result is expected.

INFERENCE: arm G as written (adversarial preload must not be able to re-export the handler or nonce) cannot pass in a shared world under any contextBridge value table, because proxying functions is the feature and the handler is reachable by platform design.

INFERENCE: a same-world preload could also alter the trusted script's behaviour by replacing the uncaptured built-ins it calls; host-side validation stays authoritative, but the script would no longer be trusted.

INFERENCE: a DOM postMessage relay from the app world through the bridge world is page-forgeable, so it would let page script send on any granted el: channel even when the preload exposed a narrower API. That is broader than Electron, where the page reaches ipcRenderer only through what the preload exposes, and broader than the section 5.1 relay rule allows.
INFERENCE: relay cost cannot flip the world choice, because the shared world fails a condition the judges called mandatory; cost only informs the relay shape.
unknowns: UNKNOWN: per-call cost of an app-world handler versus a DOM relay. This agent's relay-cost probe produced no result within 120 s in an offscreen web view and the cause was not diagnosed, so the cost is unmeasured.
UNKNOWN: how the app-world handler binds messages to the current document (reusing the host's existing per-document state versus a second nonce).
UNKNOWN: WebView2 has no isolated-world API per the F07 research note; Windows remains a divergence row and is not first-proof.

alternatives.option: A. Separate named app world for preload plus compat runtime, with a second world-scoped handler on the same per-view controller that accepts only compat (el:) envelopes; the KEL-142 handler and nonce stay unreachable by app code.
alternatives.cost: A KEL-142 spec revision (second world and handler), one more host handler path through the existing bridge owner, and an unmeasured per-call cost.
alternatives.new_invariant: App-authored renderer code never shares a content world with the trusted bridge script; the app world's capability is no broader than Electron's ipcRenderer under the window's enumerated el: grant.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: KEL-142's single-handler assumption; must not become a second transport owner or a second policy check.

alternatives.option: B. Preload in the bridge world, with contextBridge enforcing Electron's value table (maintainer position).
alternatives.cost: Measured: handler and nonce reachable by the preload and re-exportable to the page. KEL-142 AC2 becomes conditional on app code.
alternatives.new_invariant: The app preload is part of the trusted bridge base.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: KEL-142 section 5.1 and AC2 as written; the 'trusted script' premise.

alternatives.option: C. Separate app world with a nonce-less DOM relay through the bridge world.
alternatives.cost: Page script can forge relay messages, so every granted el: channel becomes page-reachable regardless of what the preload exposes.
alternatives.new_invariant: Page authority equals preload authority for compat channels.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: KEL-142 section 5.1 relay rule ('no broader shape than window.keld.invoke'); Electron's preload-as-filter contract.

alternatives.option: D. Shared world with a hardened bridge (frozen hooks, hidden handler).
alternatives.cost: Measured: the hook can be frozen but the handler cannot be hidden; it becomes an arms race inside one world.
alternatives.new_invariant: Bridge safety depends on script-level hardening holding against same-world code.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: KEL-142 AC2.

packets.decision: Whether Electron 44.4.5 runs main-process JavaScript (timers, renderer IPC, native window events) while dialog.showMessageBoxSync is open on macOS, which fixes whether Keld's parked, replay-after-return model is recorded as matching or as a divergence.
facts: FACT: dialog.md at v44.4.5 says showMessageBoxSync 'Shows a message box, it will block the process until the message box is closed' and that the window argument attaches the dialog to a parent window, 'making it modal' (raw.githubusercontent.com electron v44.4.5 docs/api/dialog.md, fetched 2026-10-06).

FACT: at v44.4.5 ShowMessageBoxSync with a visible parent calls beginSheetModalForWindow and then [NSApp runModalForWindow:window], stopping the modal from the sheet's completion handler; with no parent or a hidden parent it returns [alert runModal]. The file contains no scope that allows application tasks in a nested loop (shell/browser/ui/message_box_mac.mm at v44.4.5, fetched 2026-10-06, receipt in scratchpad/prototypes/panel-contested-receipts).

FACT: Apple documents that during runModal(for:) the app 'does not respond to any other events (including mouse, keyboard, or window-close events) unless they are associated with the window. It also does not perform any tasks (such as firing timers) that are not associated with the modal run loop' (developer.apple.com NSApplication runModal(for:), JSON endpoint fetched 2026-10-06).

FACT: Chromium's thread controller sets task_execution_allowed to false while a task runs ('Execute the task and assume the worst: it is probably not reentrant') and returns early from DoWork when application tasks are disallowed (base/task/sequence_manager/thread_controller_with_message_pump_impl.cc, chromium main branch, fetched 2026-10-06; not pinned to Electron 44's Chromium revision).

FACT: draw.io calls showMessageBoxSync inside an ipcMain handler, guards re-entry with its own modifiedModalOpen flag, and after the call uses only the returned button index (corpus drawio-desktop @2edf9fb, src/main/electron.js).
FACT (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06): KEL-237 In Progress (active owner of the lifecycle compatibility corpus); KEL-74 Done; KEL-80 Backlog.
inferences: INFERENCE: work delivered as Chromium application tasks (renderer IPC to ipcMain, libuv timers and I/O posted by Electron's Node bindings) does not run during the modal and resumes in order after it returns. This follows from the three sources above; the Node bindings file and the pinned Chromium revision were not read.

INFERENCE: events that AppKit delivers synchronously to window or app delegates (move, resize, focus, blur, app activation) may still emit into JavaScript inside the modal loop, because they do not pass through the task queue.

INFERENCE: the first-proof workflow does not depend on the answer. Keld's implementation is the same either way, and draw.io's handler does not read anything that an in-modal event could change within the single-window 4-step path. Only the scoreboard mark for the row depends on it.
unknowns: UNKNOWN: observed behaviour on Electron 44.4.5 on this Mac; no fixture has been run.
UNKNOWN: whether native delegate events emit JS during the modal.
UNKNOWN: whether the parentless [alert runModal] variant differs.

alternatives.option: C. Make E3 a first-proof gate inside PANEL-P2.
alternatives.cost: Delays F02-T3 for a result that does not change what is built.

packets.decision: How a quit request (Cmd+Q, app.quit, quitAndInstall) is sequenced against per-window close vetoes so that before-quit, per-window close, window-all-closed and will-quit match Electron 44.4.5 with two vetoing windows, and which AppKit termination reply the host uses to do it.
facts: FACT: Electron v44.4.5 overrides NSApplication terminate: and calls Browser::Quit(); the code comment says termination proceeds if all windows close and a cancelled window close aborts it (shell/browser/mac/electron_application.mm at v44.4.5, fetched 2026-10-06).
FACT: neither electron_application.mm nor electron_application_delegate.mm at v44.4.5 contains applicationShouldTerminate or any NSTerminate reply (grep of the fetched files, 2026-10-06).
FACT: Browser::Quit sets is_quitting_ from the before-quit result, then calls NotifyAndShutdown if there are no windows, otherwise WindowList::CloseAllWindows (shell/browser/browser.cc at v44.4.5).
FACT: CloseAllWindows snapshots the window list, reverses it on macOS, and calls Close() on every window without re-checking the quitting flag (shell/browser/window_list.cc at v44.4.5).
FACT: a close-event preventDefault calls WindowList::WindowCloseCancelled, and Browser::OnWindowCloseCancelled then sets is_quitting_ to false (native_window.cc and browser.cc at v44.4.5).

FACT: Browser::OnWindowAllClosed emits will-quit via NotifyAndShutdown when quitting, and otherwise emits window-all-closed (browser.cc at v44.4.5); app.md says that after Cmd+Q or app.quit the window-all-closed event 'would not be emitted'.
FACT: AutoUpdater::QuitAndInstall emits before-quit-for-update and calls CloseAllWindows directly, without Browser::Quit (shell/browser/api/electron_api_auto_updater.cc at v44.4.5).

FACT: Apple documents that returning terminateLater 'causes Cocoa to run the run loop in the NSModalPanelRunLoopMode until your app subsequently calls reply(toApplicationShouldTerminate:)' (developer.apple.com NSApplication.TerminateReply.terminateLater, JSON endpoint fetched 2026-10-06).

FACT: draw.io sets cmdQPressed in before-quit on macOS and calls app.quit() from window-all-closed when that flag is set; it clears the flag when the user cancels the unsaved-changes dialog (corpus drawio-desktop @2edf9fb, src/main/electron.js).
FACT: KEL-139 AC6 requires one ordered quit owner; no AppKit termination hook exists in the Keld host today (spec read and grep at b4b907c3, 2026-10-06).

FACT: F01-T3 (GitHub #451, two-phase quit) is blocked by F01-T1 and F02-T3; the first-proof denominator is install, activation and a 4-step workflow ending in a single-window close (publish_plan.json; panel synthesis).
FACT (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06): KEL-139 Done; KEL-96 In Progress, assignee GYLDLAB; KEL-143 Backlog.
inferences: INFERENCE (from source, no fixture run): Cmd+Q with two dirty draw.io windows in Electron 44.4.5 yields before-quit, then close on the newer window, then close on the older window (both vetoed, which cancels the quit), then the unsaved-changes dialogs, then closed for each window as the app destroys it, then window-all-closed (because the quit was cancelled), then draw.io's own app.quit, a second before-quit, will-quit and quit.

INFERENCE: this whole state machine (quitting flag, cancellation on any close veto, reverse-order close, window-all-closed suppressed while quitting) can live in the facade, because it needs only a host 'quit requested' event, the per-window close protocol and the existing ordered Quit call.

INFERENCE: Electron does not use a delayed termination reply at all, so matching it does not require NSTerminateLater. A host that returns terminateLater sits in the modal-panel run-loop mode until it replies, which may starve host work scheduled only in the default mode. This is new primary evidence against the 'later reply' mechanism clause in PANEL-D5.
INFERENCE: the first proof does not exercise quit, so it can ship without this decision.
unknowns: UNKNOWN: whether the Keld host keeps servicing Bun replies, web view callbacks and sheet presentation while AppKit holds it in the modal-panel run-loop mode after terminateLater.
UNKNOWN: behaviour on logout, restart and shutdown, where cancelling termination aborts the system action.
UNKNOWN: the recorded Electron transcript; the ordering above is source-derived only.

alternatives.option: A. Mirror Electron: the host cancels the native terminate request and emits one quit-requested event; the facade runs Electron's quit state machine; process exit happens only through the existing ordered Quit call.
alternatives.cost: The facade must reproduce the quitting flag and its cancellation rule exactly; logout/shutdown handling needs its own decision.
alternatives.new_invariant: A native terminate request never terminates the host directly; only the ordered Quit call does.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: None identified; consistent with KEL-139 AC6 one quit owner.

alternatives.option: B. Host returns terminateLater and replies after the per-window close sequence (PANEL-D5's current mechanism).
alternatives.cost: The host runs in the modal-panel run-loop mode for the whole unsaved-changes interaction; Electron does not do this, so interleaving has no oracle.
alternatives.new_invariant: The host may hold a pending AppKit termination across app-owned dialogs.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: KEL-142 rule that no UI thread blocks on Bun, if default-mode work stalls in that run-loop mode.

alternatives.option: C. Host serializes close requests per app and delivers them after any modal returns, recorded as a divergence (the panel's fallback).
alternatives.cost: Event order differs from Electron when two windows veto; draw.io's second dialog timing changes.
alternatives.new_invariant: Close events are serialized across a blocking dialog.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: Electron ordering conformance for quit.

The mempalace MCP server failed to connect (ENOENT) and was not needed.
`keld_guard::evaluate` denies every non-AppProcess principal with KELD-GUARD006 before any grant lookup (crates/keld-guard/src/lib.rs evaluate, origin/main b4b907c3).
The manifest loader ignores the top-level `windows` key (crates/keld-guard/src/lib.rs doc comment: unknown top-level keys `$schema`, `windows`, `audit` are ignored).

`DenyReason::ChannelForbidden` already renders `KELD-GUARD003: channel ... is not granted to this principal` with fix text 'Add `{channel}` to this principal's channels list in keld.permissions.jsonc', and evaluate never returns it (crates/keld-guard/src/lib.rs).
keld-core constructs no `Principal::Webview` today (grep of crates/keld-core/src at b4b907c3 returns nothing).

Arch 03 manifest example grants `"channels": ["notes.*", "el:*"]`; the same section says `**` is the only wildcard a path/URL scope has, a lone `*` matches literally, channel grants are 'a separate, not-yet-live vocabulary', and 'Channel grants connect to the schema layer: a channel's declared capability set (from .k.ts contracts) must be a subset of the caller's grants' (docs/architecture/03-security.md lines 96-98, 121-123, 172-173).

The approved KEL-102 spec lists 'Adding roles, window grants, channel grants, manifest generation' as non-goals, while its v0/destination table puts 'Per-window grants, navigation rotation, origin context, channel grants and CSP' as the destination of the webview-principal row; KEL-102-D5 makes `keld_ipc::guard_dispatch::dispatch_privileged` the sole production caller of evaluate (docs/specs/kel102-host-guard-enforcement.md lines 27-33, 88, 565).
KEL-102 is In Progress; T3 landed at 66ccbbc on 2026-10-05 and 'KEL-102 parent remains In Progress for later task units' (Linear KEL-102 status + comment cde25f5e, fetched 2026-10-06).
The Linear workspace rejects new issues: 'this workspace currently rejects creation of another Linear issue at its issue limit' (Linear KEL-102 comment 05b55d53 dated 2026-10-05, fetched 2026-10-06).

KEL-80 is Backlog; the owner comment of 2026-08-20 says 'post-v0 / YAGNI ... do not pick up' and the 2026-09-26 comment admits only a product-spine slice; its description requires 'Authorization identity is host-bound link/WebView-generation metadata, never a caller frame field' (Linear KEL-80, fetched 2026-10-06).
KEL-97 is Backlog and scoped to RoleRegistry principal binding for the app-link only (Linear KEL-97, fetched 2026-10-06). KEL-69 is Done (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06).
KEL-58 is Done: the MCP explain tool fails closed on `channel` with KELD-MCP014 (Linear KEL-58, fetched 2026-10-06; crates/keld-cli/src/mcp/permissions.rs CHANNEL_UNSUPPORTED_CODE).

KEL-208 is Done (landed fa1bfd7): the landed rule is 'a grant must name a destination'; its description records that the single-`*` glob in the arch 03 example is not a syntax the matcher implements (Linear KEL-208 description + comment ab397ba2, fetched 2026-10-06).

KEL-15 (config-schema RFC) and KEL-17 (Electron compat RFC) are Done; KEL-15 carries no attached Linear document, so no RFC text outside the repo defines the channel grammar (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06).

draw.io main registers 27 ipcMain listeners, all 27 with a string-literal channel (25 distinct literals), and has 0 invoke/handle sites; main-to-renderer channels are also literals (3 reply, 7 webContents.send) (grep of corpus drawio-desktop@2edf9fb src/main/electron.js, 2026-10-06).
The draw.io preload exposes `sendMessage(action, args)` and `registerMsgListener(action, cb)` with a page-chosen channel name (corpus drawio-desktop@2edf9fb src/main/electron-preload.js).
inferences: Because every draw.io renderer-to-main channel that can have an effect is a string-literal ipcMain registration, the first-proof grant list can be derived from main-side registrations alone; exact byte-equal literals are sufficient and no wildcard grammar is needed for the first proof.

Under exact-literal matching `el:*` grants only a channel literally named `*`, which is consistent with the existing 'lone * matches literally' rule and makes the wildcard refusal structural rather than a special case.
KEL-208's 'a grant must name a destination' is a consistent precedent for enumerated channel grants; it is an analogy about URL scopes, not proof for channels.
The crate owner is determined by existing invariants (one manifest parser and matcher in keld-guard, one evaluate caller in guard_dispatch); only the spec admission is undetermined.
unknowns: Whether the repository owner approves amending the approved KEL-102 spec (channel grants are an explicit non-goal there) or wants a separate issue once the issue cap is lifted.

Whether the draw.io webapp passes any channel to `sendMessage` that is not one of the 25 main-side literals (the webapp submodule is empty in the shallow clone); such a send would be denied with KELD-GUARD003 and have no listener under Electron either.
Whether `audit: "all"` logging of channel dispatch needs more than the channel string and byte length (it must not need an SCV decoder in keld-ipc).
How `keld migrate` will enumerate channels for apps with computed channel names (Zettlr-class; not needed for the first proof).

alternatives.option: A. Amend the KEL-102 spec: move window/channel grants from non-goal to one new scoped task unit owned by KEL-102 (keld-guard owns vocabulary, parser and KELD-GUARD003; guard_dispatch stays the sole evaluate caller). Grammar for the first proof: exact byte-equal `el:<channel>` literals per window, no wildcard.
alternatives.cost: One approved spec amendment with permission-model and public-API review gates; arch 03 example and the 'schema layer' sentence revised in the same PR; MCP explain updated in the same change.
alternatives.new_invariant: A renderer-originated application channel dispatches only when its exact channel literal is listed in `windows.<w>.channels` for the host-minted webview principal, decided solely inside dispatch_privileged, allocation-free on the allow path.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: KEL-102-D5 sole-caller rule (must be extended, not bypassed); 'no Electron-isms in keld-ipc' (the grant must be framed as generic channel-name grants); KEL-102 scope discipline (one more unit on an already long-running issue).

alternatives.option: B. New Linear issue and new spec dedicated to window/channel grants.
alternatives.cost: Cannot be created today (workspace at its issue cap); the first proof waits on an owner action to free capacity; F04-T3 stays blocked meanwhile.
alternatives.new_invariant: Same as A, with a separate spec file as the owner.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: None additional; risk is a second document describing guard dispatch that drifts from the KEL-102 spec.

alternatives.option: C. KEL-80 owns it as part of the bridge contract.
alternatives.cost: KEL-80 is Backlog and owner-parked except for a product-spine slice; it would mix permission policy into a transport/backpressure issue.
alternatives.new_invariant: Channel authorization defined by the bridge owner.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: One rule, one owner: guard policy would be specified outside the guard owner; one concern per issue.

alternatives.option: D. No evaluator for the first proof (treat el: traffic like today's ungated echo, or allowlist in the facade).
alternatives.cost: Zero now.
alternatives.new_invariant: None.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: Default-deny is sacred; contradicts the resolved map decision that the enumerated per-window grant is the only renderer-to-main boundary. Rejected.

packets.recommendation: Option A. The crate owner is already determined by evidence (keld-guard for vocabulary/parser/deny code, guard_dispatch for evaluation), KEL-102 is the only live owner whose own destination table names per-window and channel grants, and a new issue cannot be created today. Ship the narrowest grammar: exact-literal `el:<channel>` entries only, KELD-GUARD003 on miss, `keld migrate` refuses any wildcard; revise the arch 03 example to enumerated literals and scope the 'declared capability set' sentence to schema channels in the same PR. Fold the F04-A4 generation contract into the same amendment so the webview principal is specified once. The single remaining question for the owner: do you approve amending the KEL-102 spec to admit exact-literal `windows.<w>.channels` grants for webview principals as a new KEL-102 task unit, instead of waiting for a separate issue?
packets.falsifier: Any of: (1) a first-proof draw.io workflow step needs a renderer-to-main channel that is not a string literal in the main source, so exact-literal grants cannot express it; (2) the channel check cannot be placed in dispatch_privileged without an allocation on the allow path or without Electron-specific knowledge in keld-ipc; (3) the owner declines the KEL-102 amendment.
packets.reversible: yes - the ownership record is a spec/Linear change, and exact-literal matching is strictly narrower than any later glob grammar, so widening later is additive; starting with a glob and narrowing later would break shipped manifests.
packets.missing_evidence: The owner's exact-content approval of the KEL-102 amendment text; a scan of the populated draw.io webapp for channel names passed to `sendMessage`/`registerMsgListener` at the pinned commit.
packets.next_action: Orchestrator (single Linear writer) posts this packet as a comment on KEL-102 with the one question; on a yes, the KEL-102 spec author drafts the amendment. First observable completion check: a KEL-102 comment id recording the approval, then a fixture where an ungranted channel from a page returns KELD-GUARD003 and deleting the grant check makes that fixture fail.
packets.owner: KEL-102 (In Progress; Linear, fetched 2026-10-06) with crates keld-guard and keld-ipc guard_dispatch; the admission itself is a repository-owner approval.

packets.decision: Whether a contextBridge-exposed function can return its value synchronously across WKWebView content worlds (and later WebKitGTK), or whether exposed functions are Promise-returning with a labelled divergence.
facts: Every function draw.io exposes (`request`, `registerMsgListener`, `sendMessage`, `listenOnce`) returns undefined; the second exposed key is a plain value object `{type, versions}`; page functions are passed in as arguments, including one nested inside an object (`msg.listener`) (corpus drawio-desktop@2edf9fb src/main/electron-preload.js).
draw.io has 0 `sendSync(` sites (grep of corpus drawio-desktop@2edf9fb src, 2026-10-06).

Zettlr's preload exposes functions whose return value is consumed synchronously: `ipc.on()` returns an unsubscribe function, `config.get()` returns a sendSync result, `getCitationCallback()` returns a function that itself returns a sendSync result (corpus zettlr@e6c7fd8 source/common/modules/preload/index.ts lines 28-80).
The live macOS bridge relays between the page world and an isolated content world; the published plan lists F04-A3 as a blocker of F04-T4 (publish_plan.json F04-T4 blocked_by).
KEL-142 (owner of the bridge seam) is Done as of 2026-10-01 (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06).
inferences: The first proof does not need a synchronous cross-world return: draw.io's exposed functions are void, so an ordered asynchronous relay with function proxies in both directions satisfies it. F04-T4's draw.io slice should not be blocked by this ticket; only the Zettlr sync-return cells are.
A shared-DOM relay is plausible because DOM event dispatch is synchronous and both worlds see the same DOM; this is unverified on WKWebView.

With an asynchronous relay, successive calls keep their order but a call followed immediately by unload could be lost where Electron would have sent it; no draw.io workflow step is known to depend on that.
unknowns: Whether an isolated-world listener runs synchronously inside a page-world `dispatchEvent` on WKWebView.
What `CustomEvent.detail` carries across worlds (null, a clone, or a shared object) and whether any JS object identity leaks.
Per-call cost of a DOM-string relay versus the asynchronous relay.
WebKitGTK behaviour (needs a Linux machine).

alternatives.option: A. Shared-DOM synchronous relay (page dispatches a DOM event; the preload world's listener writes the serialized result to shared DOM state the page reads back).
alternatives.cost: A small WKWebView experiment, then serialization of every call through DOM strings; a second call path beside the asynchronous relay.
alternatives.new_invariant: Cross-world values travel only as serialized strings; no JS object or function identity crosses worlds.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: KEL-142 isolation rule that the page must not reach the native handler or document nonce (the relay must carry neither).

alternatives.option: B. Asynchronous-only exposure: every exposed function returns a Promise; labelled divergence with a compat diagnostic.
alternatives.cost: Zettlr's sync-return functions break without source edits; draw.io is unaffected.
alternatives.new_invariant: Exposed functions are never synchronous on isolated-world engines.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: KEL-127 direction 'never a silent downgrade' if the label or diagnostic is missing.

alternatives.option: C. Run the app preload in the page world to get synchronous calls for free.
alternatives.cost: Gives up engine isolation that exists today.
alternatives.new_invariant: None.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: KEL-142/KEL-139 isolation acceptance. Rejected.

packets.recommendation: Park for the first proof and remove the F04-A3 edge from F04-T4's draw.io slice (asynchronous relay with void-return functions). Before any Zettlr work, run the smallest experiment on a macOS WKWebView harness with two content worlds. Arms: (1) page calls `dispatchEvent` and reads the result in the same task with no await - sync return observed or not; (2) negative control - the same assertion over a `postMessage` relay must fail; (3) leak check - an object and a function placed in `detail` must not be reachable or callable from the other world; (4) re-entrancy - a preload listener calling back into a page listener during the call preserves order; (5) cost - 10,000 calls at 64 B and 4 KiB, p50/p99 recorded as a diagnostic. Exit: arms 1, 3 and 4 pass and arm 2 fails as designed gives option A; arm 1 failing gives option B as a labelled divergence. WebKitGTK is a separate Linux observation.
packets.falsifier: The populated draw.io webapp reads a return value from a `window.electron.*` call or depends on a send completing before a synchronous unload; or arm 3 shows a shared object identity across worlds, which would make option A an isolation regression.
packets.reversible: yes - parking changes nothing in the tree; the relay is an internal detail behind `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld`, so moving between A and B later changes only compat cells.
packets.missing_evidence: The experiment transcript on real WKWebView (arms 1-5); a scan of the populated draw.io webapp for uses of return values from `window.electron.*`.
packets.next_action: Orchestrator edits the map: drop F04-A3 from F04-T4's first-proof blockers and mark this ticket as Zettlr-gated. First observable completion check: F04-T4's blocked-by list for the draw.io slice no longer names F04-A3.

packets.decision: Which single owner mints the navigation generation consumed by the bridge, the guard webview principal and senderFrame/reply semantics, and at which point it rotates.
facts: The bridge keeps a private `navigation_generation: u64` per WebView, stamps it on every admitted renderer request (documented there as the 'host-owned navigation generation that admitted this call') and settles replies only for the matching generation (crates/keld-wv/src/wkwebview/macos_bridge.rs, origin/main b4b907c3).
That counter rotates in two places: when the host calls the engine's navigate, and on wry `PageLoadEvent::Started` (crates/keld-wv/src/wkwebview/mod.rs).

wry 0.56.1 (the Cargo.lock pin) emits `PageLoadEvent::Started` from WKNavigationDelegate `webView:didCommitNavigation:` (wry-0.56.1 src/wkwebview/navigation.rs). So engine-observed rotation is at commit, not provisional start, and one host-initiated navigation rotates twice.
The guard principal is `Principal::Webview { id, generation: u32 }`; live media backends mint generation 0 (crates/keld-guard/src/lib.rs; crates/keld-wv/src/media.rs WEBVIEW_MEDIA_GENERATION).

The approved KEL-102 spec says the webview caller is 'created and rotated only by the host webview/navigation registry' and 'Current backends use generation 0; a later navigation registry must increment it before a post-navigation request can dispatch' (docs/specs/kel102-host-guard-enforcement.md lines 399, 414-416).

The KEL-142 spec binds the document nonce to `(WebviewId, navigation generation)` and requires that 'provisional/new navigation invalidates the previous nonce before the new document may dispatch' (docs/specs/kel142-macos-renderer-bridge-api.md §5.2 items 3 and 6). It does not pin an integer width.
Neither the KEL-142 nor the KEL-139 spec, nor the bridge code, mentions same-document navigation (grep for same-document/hashchange/fragment/pushState, 2026-10-06).

draw.io checks `event.senderFrame` in `validateSender` (null means reject, otherwise URL prefix match) before acting on renderer messages, and replies with `event.reply` (corpus drawio-desktop@2edf9fb src/main/electron.js).
KEL-102 is In Progress, KEL-142 is Done, KEL-143 is Backlog (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06).
inferences: The ticket's premise 'rotated on navigation start' is only half right: for renderer-initiated navigations the live rotation is at commit, which already matches Electron's frame-bound reply semantics and leaves a cancelled provisional navigation's document usable.

Because the first proof dispatches renderer channels under a webview principal (F04-A1), the KEL-102 sentence forbids doing so with a constant generation 0; unification is therefore a first-proof requirement, not polish.
WKWebView does not call didCommitNavigation for same-document (fragment/history) navigations, so the live code probably does not rotate on a hash change; this is unverified.
A new keld-core registry type is not needed for the first proof: one live mint already exists and already travels with each request.
unknowns: Whether a same-document navigation on WKWebView triggers the commit callback (would drop replies Electron delivers).
Whether a host-initiated load that fails before commit leaves the previous document with an invalidated nonce and no way to re-bind.
Whether the populated draw.io webapp mutates `location.hash` during the 4-step workflow.

alternatives.option: A. The existing per-WebView host navigation state is the single mint; the guard webview principal for channel dispatch is built from the generation stamped on the admitted request, never from a constant. Rotation: cross-document commit, plus host-initiated load request as an earlier fail-closed invalidation; never on same-document navigation. Width follows the approved KEL-102 spec (u32) with a checked increment that fails closed on exhaustion.
alternatives.cost: A contract paragraph in the KEL-102 amendment (same unit as F04-A1), a narrowing of the bridge counter's type, and three conformance fixtures.
alternatives.new_invariant: For any dispatched renderer request, the generation that admitted it, the generation in the guard principal and the generation deciding senderFrame nullability and reply delivery are the same value from one mint.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: KEL-142's public request accessor type changes (public-API gate on keld-wv); the media path keeps constant 0 until KEL-102's media unit adopts the same source, which must be recorded as a named residual.

alternatives.option: B. Lift the counter into a new keld-core window/webview registry now and make both the bridge and the guard consume it.
alternatives.cost: A new registry type and a cross-crate callback from the engine page-load handler, built for one live WebView.
alternatives.new_invariant: keld-core owns all webview identity state.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: YAGNI for the first proof; risk of an unexercised abstraction. This remains the destination when a second consumer (media rotation, multiple webviews) needs it.

alternatives.option: C. Keep two counters and document a mapping.
alternatives.cost: None now.
alternatives.new_invariant: None.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: One rule, one owner; senderFrame nullability and guard revocation can disagree. Rejected.

alternatives.option: D. Rotate at provisional start for all navigations.
alternatives.cost: Engine delegate work to observe provisional start.
alternatives.new_invariant: Earlier invalidation.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: A cancelled navigation (draw.io prevents navigations) would strand the live document without a bridge; diverges from Electron, which keeps the old frame until commit. Rejected.

packets.recommendation: Option A, recorded in the same KEL-102 amendment as F04-A1. Evidence determines both halves: the approved specs already name the host navigation state as the only minter, the code already has exactly one rotating counter, and commit is both the live engine-observed rotation point and Electron's frame boundary. Add three conformance entries to F04-T1: stale reply after cross-document navigation is dropped; a hash change during a pending request does not drop the reply; a cancelled renderer-initiated navigation keeps the bridge usable.
packets.falsifier: Any of: a hash or pushState change on WKWebView rotates the generation; a cancelled provisional navigation invalidates the document nonce; a dispatch is observed where the bridge-stamped generation differs from the guard principal's generation (negative control: a mutation that rotates only one must fail the fixture).
packets.reversible: yes - the mint is private host state behind the request accessor; lifting it into a keld-core registry later (option B) changes no wire format or manifest.
packets.missing_evidence: One real-macOS observation of same-document navigation and of a failed host-initiated load against the live bridge; these are fixtures inside F04-T1, not a separate research task.
packets.next_action: KEL-102 spec author adds the generation contract to the F04-A1 amendment draft; F04-T1 author lands the three conformance entries. First observable completion check: a fixture shows one navigation producing the same generation in the admitted request and the guard principal, and fails when only one of the two is rotated.
packets.owner: KEL-102 (In Progress; Linear, fetched 2026-10-06) for the webview-principal contract; crate keld-wv for the mint (KEL-142, Done).

packets.decision: Whether renderer `ipcRenderer.sendSync` can be implemented on WKWebView as a deadline-bounded blocking call using a synchronous XMLHttpRequest to a host scheme handler, or stays a scaffolded typed throw.
facts: draw.io has 0 `sendSync(` sites (grep of corpus drawio-desktop@2edf9fb src, 2026-10-06).

Zettlr's preload calls `ipcRenderer.sendSync` behind synchronously-returning exposed functions (`ipc.sendSync`, `config.get`, `config.set`, the citation callback) (corpus zettlr@e6c7fd8 source/common/modules/preload/index.ts lines 37, 57, 63, 74).

KEL-127 delegated direction 5: 'Async-first native APIs do not authorize pretending asynchronous calls preserve synchronous Electron semantics'; direction 4 requires explicit diagnostics, 'never a silent downgrade' (Linear KEL-127, status Todo, fetched 2026-10-06).

KEL-142's Linear text forbids 'a second renderer-routing protocol'; KEL-79's acceptance says its loopback listener 'is not used for Keld IPC' (Linear KEL-142 Done and KEL-79 Backlog, fetched 2026-10-06).

An existing scratch harness already registers a WKURLSchemeHandler and loads a page from it; it exercises fetch only, not synchronous XHR (scratchpad wayfinder/electron-compat/probes/f05-wk-scheme/main.swift).
The map already records sendSync as scaffolded until this experiment passes and ranks it third among program risks, Zettlr-gated (panel/synthesis.md).
inferences: The first proof ships without this decision: draw.io never calls sendSync, and its one blocking call (`showMessageBoxSync`) is main-process and belongs to PANEL-P1.
The experiment is independent of PANEL-P1: for renderer sendSync the Bun main is not parked; it answers an ordinary call when `returnValue` is set.

The deadline must be enforced by the host failing the scheme task, because browsers forbid setting a timeout on a synchronous XHR from a document; this is from memory of the XHR standard and needs a receipt.
A scheme-handler lane is a second renderer-to-host carriage unless its body is the same bridge envelope bound to the document nonce; admitting it needs an amendment by the bridge owner.
unknowns: Whether WKWebView services a synchronous XHR to a WKURLSchemeHandler-backed scheme at all, and on which host thread the handler runs while the page is blocked.
Whether POST bodies reach the scheme handler intact at 64 B, 4 KiB and 64 KiB.
Whether cross-origin rules block the request from the app's page origin and which response headers are required.
Behaviour when the webview navigates or is destroyed during a blocked request.
Electron's observable when `returnValue` is never set (a refuter derived `{ error: 'reply was never sent' }` from source; not re-verified here).
WebKitGTK and WebView2 equivalents.

alternatives.option: A. Synchronous XHR to a host scheme handler carrying the existing bridge envelope, nonce-bound, with a host-enforced deadline and rate limit.
alternatives.cost: The experiment, then an amendment by the bridge owner (and KEL-79 if its transport is reused) plus wire-protocol and public-API gates.
alternatives.new_invariant: Exactly one synchronous renderer-to-host lane exists; it carries the same envelope and identity checks as the asynchronous lane and always terminates by reply or deadline.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: 'No second renderer-routing protocol' (KEL-142); KEL-142's rule that no host UI thread blocks on Bun.

alternatives.option: B. Keep sendSync scaffolded: typed throw with a fix-it pointing to invoke, labelled divergence.
alternatives.cost: Zettlr-class apps need source edits; no engine work.
alternatives.new_invariant: sendSync never blocks and never silently becomes asynchronous.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: Arch 02 §5 statement that sendSync 'must exist' stays unmet for those apps.

alternatives.option: C. Silent Promise rewrite or busy-wait polling.
alternatives.cost: None.
alternatives.new_invariant: None.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: KEL-127 directions 4 and 5. Rejected.

packets.recommendation: Park until Zettlr work is scheduled; keep option B as the live state. When scheduled, extend the existing scheme-handler harness with these arms: (1) immediate reply - does the synchronous XHR complete, and is the handler called on the host main thread while the page is blocked; RTT p50/p99 over 1,000 calls; (2) reply after a 50 ms host-side hop - proves the host run loop keeps running; (3) no reply, host fails the task at a deadline - page sees an exception within the deadline; (4) body integrity at 64 B, 4 KiB, 64 KiB; (5) cross-origin request from the app page origin; (6) navigate or destroy the webview mid-request - no hang or crash; (7) negative control - an asynchronous message-handler call cannot produce the value in the same task; (8) record the Electron 44.4.5 observable for a never-set `returnValue`. Exit: arms 1-4 and 6 pass gives option A as a candidate for the bridge owner's amendment, with the rate limit derived from the measured p99; any of them failing keeps option B.
packets.falsifier: A first-proof draw.io path that reaches `ipcRenderer.sendSync` (would move this to first-proof); or arm 1 showing WKWebView refuses or deadlocks on synchronous XHR to a custom scheme (kills option A on macOS).
packets.reversible: yes - parking leaves the scaffolded throw in place; adopting option A later adds a lane without changing existing asynchronous behaviour.
packets.missing_evidence: The experiment transcript on real macOS WKWebView (arms 1-8); primary receipts for the XHR synchronous-timeout rule and for WKURLSchemeHandler request-body delivery.
packets.next_action: Orchestrator marks this ticket parked (Zettlr-gated) on the map and links the harness path as the starting point. First observable completion check: the map row for F04-A5 shows 'parked - Zettlr-gated' with the eight arms listed.

packets.decision: Under the strict profile, `userData` and `logs` live inside the KEL-78 reviewed role-private container, where raw synchronous `node:fs` works by OS containment with no guard grant; a `node:fs`-over-FsBroker facade is not the owner of `userData`.
facts: FACT: The approved KEL-78 spec says a guard allow MUST NOT widen the child's OS profile, and its authority table has the row 'Files outside a reviewed role-private container | deny'. Source: <keld repo>/docs/specs/kel78-strict-profile-sandbox.md, section 'Authority surface the profile must cover', read at main b4b907c3.

FACT: The same spec requires role-private path success as a positive control ('create/read of a role-private path succeeds'), and its Linux candidate must 'still allow the role-private paths that role is supposed to use'. Source: kel78-strict-profile-sandbox.md, Linux candidate item 2 and the test-matrix row 'Direct filesystem'.
FACT: The Linux strict launcher already bind-mounts a role root read-write into the sandbox (`--bind role_root /app`). Source: <keld repo>/crates/keld-runtime/src/linux_strict.rs (SANDBOX_ROLE_ROOT).

INFERENCE: if consent is admitted, the zero-new-grammar spelling is a separate capability node (operation shell.confirm, resource = canonical scheme literal) evaluated by the existing matcher, with the host asking the guard twice (literal first, then confirm class).
INFERENCE: a 'legacy only' option does not exist as a clean path: brokers stay guarded under legacy, and having the facade spawn the OS opener from Bun would be a second policy path.

alternatives.option: A. Exact literal origins only; every other URL is a KELD-GUARD002 rejection reported as a declared divergence.

alternatives.new_invariant: A user decision at call time can authorize a destination the reviewed manifest did not name.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: Manifest-as-lockfile reviewability; prompt fatigue as a security control; arch 03 has no consent owner today.

alternatives.new_invariant: A grant may delegate the authority to the caller.

UNKNOWN: whether Keld's userData path for a migrated app resolves to the Electron app's existing directory (electron-store state would then carry over while web storage does not).

alternatives.invariant_at_risk: KEL-127 data-integrity expectation if an in-place upgrade is ever claimed without the disclosure.

alternatives.option: B. One-shot host-side import from the Chromium session store.
alternatives.cost: Chromium storage-format parsers in the host (dependency gate, format drift per Chromium version), three engine-specific writers, IndexedDB and cookies each separate.
alternatives.new_invariant: The privileged host parses third-party browser profile formats.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: Std-first minimal dependencies; one-parser rule; KEL-135 'accepts no old-root input'; host attack surface.

alternatives.option: C. App-assisted export in the bridge release, replayed by a host-injected first-launch seed before page scripts.
alternatives.cost: Requires the bridge release; per-app key list; exactly-once marker; depends on the final origin (KEL-79).
alternatives.new_invariant: A first-launch seed script with an exactly-once guarantee in the preload ordering contract.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: Preload ordering contract; coupling to the unowned origin decision.

Reject B. Record C as the only import shape worth specifying, and only when an in-place upgrade (the arch 04 bridge release) is actually scheduled. Correct the ticket text so it no longer attributes the loss to the origin change alone.

packets.reversible: Yes, as long as the new invariant holds (Electron session data untouched). After users create new state under Keld, a later import becomes a merge rather than a copy.
packets.missing_evidence: None needed for the decision. For a future C: the KEL-79 origin decision and a bridge-release schedule. Separately, the file:// localStorage persistence observable on WKWebView for the first-proof fixture.

inferences: INFERENCE: Zettlr uses the environment as a main-to-renderer data channel (main sets values at runtime, later-spawned renderers inherit them). The faithful source would be the main role's environment at window creation, not the host's, so a host-side 'NODE_ENV only' list serves neither corpus app.
INFERENCE: copying the main role's environment into the page would hand the app-link possession secret and the user's shell environment to an untrusted webview principal.

INFERENCE (not executed): with env absent or empty, Zettlr's preload does not throw (Object.assign skips an undefined source); its Debug tab shows 'not available' and the tray preference loses its disabled state.
unknowns: UNKNOWN: whether pinned Electron 44.4.5 sandboxed renderers see main-process environment mutations made after app start (snapshot at renderer spawn versus at launch).
UNKNOWN: whether any committed Zettlr denominator cell will depend on the five names (no Zettlr denominator exists).
UNKNOWN: whether the legacy profile will change environment inheritance for the Bun role.

alternatives.option: A. process.env is an empty object in every preload; the migrate report lists each renderer-side environment read with the names read.
alternatives.cost: Zettlr: three version strings read 'not available' and the tray-preference state is wrong (declared divergence). No new mechanism.

alternatives.invariant_at_risk: None for Keld; must be reported, not silent (KEL-127 direction item 4).

alternatives.option: B. Declared name allow-list (compat config); values snapshotted from the main role's environment at window creation and delivered with the host-synthesized process descriptor; KELD_* names excluded unconditionally.
alternatives.cost: New compat config key (public-API gate), a descriptor field, an exclusion rule with a negative control, approved spec.
alternatives.new_invariant: Only declared names flow, only from the app's own main role to its own windows, never KELD_*.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: One-owner rule (information-flow policy declared outside the permissions manifest); possession-secret leak if the exclusion fails.

alternatives.option: C. Copy the whole environment (Electron parity).
alternatives.cost: None to build.
alternatives.new_invariant: Untrusted pages can read the role's bootstrap secret and the user's environment.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: arch 03 principal model; app-link possession-secret confidentiality.

alternatives.option: D. Fixed built-in list such as NODE_ENV only.
alternatives.cost: Hard-coded policy in the shim with no corpus consumer.
alternatives.new_invariant: A host-chosen environment vocabulary.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: YAGNI; one policy owner.
