Reject C and D. Specify B only when a committed Zettlr cell reads one of the five names, and then source values from the main role (not the host) with unconditional KELD_* exclusion and a negative control. The first-proof renderer shim should define process.env as an empty object so the field exists.

inferences: Electron emits app and window lifecycle events on the browser main thread, so a main-only fixture is expected to be order-stable. Nobody has observed this.
The first BrowserWindow id is probably the same on every fresh process, so a window-id normaliser may be unnecessary, and an unnecessary normaliser can hide a divergence.
Ten identical runs bound the per-run flip rate only below roughly 26% at 95% confidence; thirty bound it below roughly 10%. Ten runs alone is weak evidence of determinism.
A single merged order of main and renderer rows will vary in Electron itself (the X01 semantics refuter's finding), so cross-process comparison needs explicit causal edges.

It is first-proof because #419's diff against an unreplicated Electron transcript cannot tell a Keld divergence from Electron's own run-to-run variance. Only the main-process, macOS part is first-proof; the renderer ordering rule belongs to the X01-T1 spec and is next.
unknowns: Whether the ordered main-process sequence is identical across runs.
Which raw fields actually vary (pid, monotonic time, absolute paths, Error.stack, window id).
Whether rows that originate in the renderer interleave stably with main rows.
Whether the Cmd+Q route (AppKit terminate) orders events like app.quit(). Out of scope here; #419 owns it.
The X01 invariants refuter reported that the LineLog timeout panics without killing the child process. Not re-checked here.

1. Role
Run one bounded determinism experiment on the pinned Electron binary and report observations. You do not own the harness design, the comparator, any Keld code, any golden file or the decision text.

2. Goal
A receipt stating, for Electron 44.4.5 on macOS arm64, whether the main-process quit-order transcript is identical across repeated runs, and the minimal set of fields that had to be normalised to make it so.

3. Success criteria
- SC1: every arm A and B run exits 0 with a complete transcript ending in the quit row and the process exit code. A killed or incomplete run is reported, never retried silently.
- SC2: verdict DETERMINISTIC only if all 30 arm A and B normalised sequences share one SHA-256. Otherwise NONDETERMINISTIC, listing each distinct sequence, its count and the first differing row pair. State the bound: zero flips in 30 runs bounds the per-run flip rate only below about 10% at 95% confidence.
- SC3: doc cross-check, quoting the app.md sentences in the receipt. In every arm A and B run, before-quit precedes the first window close, will-quit follows the last window closed, quit is last, and window-all-closed is absent. In every arm C run, window-all-closed is present. A violation is a finding, not something to normalise.
- SC4: the normaliser list is minimal. Each entry names one field path and cites the observed raw diff that requires it. A candidate with no observed variance (for example the window id) is listed as not needed.
- SC5: negative controls. Swapping two rows in a copy of one transcript changes its hash; changing one event name changes the hash after normalisation; arm C shows the event arm A asserts absent.
- All evidence is real-OS (macOS arm64). Nothing here is a Keld conformance claim.

4. Prerequisites
- Network access to GitHub releases; about 250 MB free disk; a logged-in GUI session.
- No approval is needed: there are no repo, GitHub or Linear writes.
- Read KEL-237 and its comments first. If an unexpired claim there covers Electron recorder work, stop.

5. Resources
- Fixture directory: package.json with type module and main main.js; main.js (ESM); index.html (static). For arm D only add preload.cjs (CommonJS, require('electron')).
- Register every listener synchronously at top level before any await (esm.md: the app may be ready before the entry point finishes).
- Emit one line per event with fs.writeSync(1, ...): seq (process-local counter), proc, kind, name, args as JSON, plus raw pid, monotonic time, window id and any paths.
- Log: will-finish-launching, ready, browser-window-created, did-finish-load, before-quit, window close, window closed, window-all-closed, will-quit, quit with its exit code.
- Trigger: call app.quit() inside the did-finish-load handler. No timers, no sleeps.
- Electron: download the darwin-arm64 zip, verify its sha256 against the PIN, extract it outside the fixture directory and run the binary directly with the fixture path. Do not use npx (it downloads lazily at record time). Keep ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE unset and record the environment.
- Each run is a child process with stdout, stderr and exit code captured and a 60-second kill switch.
- Arms: A = 10 cold sequential runs on an idle machine. B = 20 runs under CPU contention (one busy process per logical core, started before and stopped after; a perturbation, not a synchronisation aid). C = 10 runs of the control variant that calls win.close() and has a window-all-closed listener that logs and then quits. D (report-only) = 10 runs of arm A plus a renderer that sends two ipcRenderer.send markers which main logs on receipt.
- Normalisation: start with an empty set. Hash the ordered rows (proc, kind, name, args) per run. For each field that differs between runs, add one named normaliser for that exact field path and re-hash. Never normalise event name, kind, order, Error.message or exit code.

6. Delegation
None.

7. Verification
- Electron --version prints v44.4.5 and the zip digest equals the PIN.
- SHA256SUMS over the receipt verifies.
- The per-run hash table and the three negative-control outputs are pasted into RECEIPT.txt.

8. Output
One keld.execution-artifact/v1 JSON with status passed, findings, os-unavailable or hard-failure. Evidence rows: the verdict, the distinct-sequence table, the normaliser list with justifications, the arm C control, the arm D observation (stable or unstable interleave and which rows), machine identity and every command with its exit code. The dispatcher posts the result on gyldlab/keld#411; #419 and #494 consume it.

9. Stop rules
- Zip digest mismatch: stop, hard-failure.
- No GUI session: stop, os-unavailable.
- A run that needs a sleep or a retry to complete: stop and report.
- The same step failing after two attempts: stop and report.
- Any need to edit the keld repo, or to normalise order or event names to reach one hash: stop and report as a finding.
- A claim conflict on KEL-237: stop.

proto.question:
Does a host-owned window model reproduce Electron BrowserWindow/WebContents observable lifecycle (ready-to-show, show, close with preventDefault, closed, destroy, isDestroyed, window-all-closed default quit, app.quit: before-quit -> per-window close -> will-quit -> quit) while the Bun role can crash and be replaced without the window disappearing?

Answer from the model: yes for every listed sequence, with one exception and several open gaps. 117/117 scripted expectations hold, and 17 single-mutation negative controls (closed before tombstone, host auto-close on timeout, window-all-closed during quit, destroy() asking for close, veto not cancelling quit, crash destroying every window, and others) each make a check fail. This is a model check, not OS evidence.

The exception: under the map text as written (PANEL-D5, F02-T3: "the host closes a window on its own only when the generation is revoked"), a window with an unanswered CloseRequested does disappear when Bun crashes. Its veto listener never ran, so the page that KEL-143 recovery would otherwise have preserved is lost. Windows with no pending close survive and are re-adopted.

proto.module_shape:
One self-contained HTML file (93.5 KB, no external resources) with three script blocks.

1. `<script id="logic">` defines `KeldWindowLifecycle`, a pure reducer over plain-JSON state.
   - API: `initialState(options)`, `dispatch(state, action) -> {state, result:{ok, error, value, entries}}`, `dispatchAll(state, actions)` (several calls in one Bun tick, before any host event is processed), `getAllWindows`, `liveWindows`, `invariants`, plus `CATALOGUE` (32 actions), `ERRORS`, `OPTION_VALUES`, `DESTROYED_TEXT`.
   - State: host (phase, quit record, retired generations, owed LastWindowClosed), bun (generation, alive/parked/dead, unhealthy flag, isQuitting), app listener settings, the host window registry, the current generation's facade objects, the host-to-Bun inbox, in-flight renderer invokes, and an ordered transcript.
   - A `pump` delivers queued host events only while the Bun main thread is alive, which is what makes parked and crashed states observable.
   - Two model options carry the open decisions: `pendingCloseOnRevoke` (host-closes | keep-window) and `quitSweep` (all-at-once | serialized).

2. `<script id="scenarios">` defines `KeldWindowLifecycleScenarios`: 33 scripted steps in three tabs, each with expectation functions, plus `runStep` and `runAll`, shared by the page and the headless check.

3. `<script id="page">` is rendering only.

Blocks 1 and 2 were executed in an empty Node vm context (no window, document, console or timers), so they are DOM-free.
scenarios: HAPPY 1-6: Ready(g1) with zero windows; new BrowserWindow({show:false}); hidden first paint -> ready-to-show; win.show() -> show; user close vetoed by preventDefault (window kept); then win.close() -> close, tombstone, closed, window-all-closed, default app.quit() -> before-quit, will-quit, quit.
HAPPY 7: app.quit() with two windows -> before-quit, w2:close, w1:close, w2:closed, w1:closed, will-quit, quit; no window-all-closed.

HAPPY 8-10: Bun g1 crashes with a visible painted window -> the window stays and all facade objects are gone; successor g2 gets WindowAdopted then Ready, getAllWindows() returns w1 with the same (w1, wg1); g2 closes it normally.

EDGE 1-4: close clicked while Bun is parked -> CloseRequested seq 1 unanswered; two deadline periods pass -> no auto-close, role flagged unhealthy; second click coalesces (2 attempts, 1 request); unpark -> close emitted once, vetoed, window kept.
EDGE 5: destroy() after a vetoed close -> no close event from destroy, closed exactly once.
EDGE 6: win.close() twice in one tick -> one closed; one close in this model (Electron may emit close per attempt: open).

EDGE 7-8: app.quit() with w2 vetoing -> every window asked, w1 closes, quit cancelled, no will-quit, app.quit() callable again; then Cmd+Q with before-quit preventDefault -> applicationShouldTerminate later, reply NO, no window asked.
EDGE 9: Cmd+Q that goes through -> same app-visible order as app.quit(); hooks are applicationShouldTerminate then reply YES; windowShouldClose never runs.
EDGE 10: will-quit vetoed -> app alive with zero windows and no window-all-closed; second app.quit() emits before-quit again, then will-quit, quit.
EDGE 11: serialized sweep option, three windows, middle one vetoes -> w3 closes, w2 vetoes, w1 is never asked (differs from Electron's all-windows sweep).

EDGE 12-13: crash with an in-flight ipcRenderer.invoke and an unanswered close -> invoke rejected exactly once with an ambiguous-outcome error and never replayed; host closes w1 (map text), w2 survives; g2 adopts only w2, with no close listener.
EDGE 14: same crash under keep-window -> both windows survive, the close request is released, the invoke is still rejected once.
ILLEGAL 1-3: after closed, win.getBounds() throws TypeError 'Object has been destroyed'; isDestroyed() returns true without throwing; show(), close(), destroy() each throw and send nothing.
ILLEGAL 4: new BrowserWindow with nodeIntegration -> typed KELD-COMPAT error, no window minted.
ILLEGAL 5: a page sends a window command to the host -> KELD-GUARD006, window unaffected.
ILLEGAL 6: Bun sends CloseAllow with a seq nobody asked for -> typed KELD-IPC error, window stays.
ILLEGAL 7: facade call while Bun is parked -> PROTOTYPE-PRECONDITION (no actor); user close plus three periods -> window still open.

ILLEGAL 8-9: invoke with no live generation -> immediate ambiguous-outcome rejection; retired generation reconnects with its old token -> KELD-IPC-007; successor has no object at all for a window destroyed before it was admitted.
decisions_encoded: FACT (Electron v44.4.5 browser-window.md): close fires before DOM beforeunload/unload and preventDefault cancels; destroy() emits no close and guarantees closed; ready-to-show fires when the page has rendered while not shown.
FACT (electron_api_base_window.cc:171-184): MarkDestroyed() runs before Emit('closed'), so isDestroyed() is true inside the closed listener.

FACT (gin_helper/function_template.h:215-216, base-window.md:607): destroyed member access throws a TypeError with the exact text 'Object has been destroyed'. PANEL-D6 fixed the text only; the TypeError class is a new receipt.

FACT (app.md, lib/browser/init.ts:169-173, browser.cc OnWindowAllClosed): window-all-closed default is app.quit() when the app has no listener, so the default quit is itself cancellable at before-quit; it is not emitted for Cmd+Q or app.quit().

FACT (browser.cc Quit/NotifyAndShutdown/OnWindowCloseCancelled, window_list.cc:78-88): before-quit, then every window is asked (reverse order on macOS), then will-quit, then quit; any window veto cancels the quit but the other windows still close; a second app.quit() mid-quit returns early.
FACT (browser.cc): after a vetoed will-quit, the next app.quit() emits before-quit again. The F01 refuter oracle wording ('without a second before-quit->close cycle') is ambiguous against this.

FACT (electron_ns_window_delegate.mm:411-414, electron_application.mm:92-101): Electron returns NO from windowShouldClose: and its Cmd+Q path overrides terminate: to call Browser::Quit(). It does not use applicationShouldTerminate.
FACT (Apple docs, fetched 2026-10-06): windowShouldClose is not called on quit; NSTerminateLater makes Cocoa run the run loop in a modal-panel mode until the reply.
FACT (Keld b4b907c3): no windowShouldClose/applicationShouldTerminate hook exists in keld-wv or keld-core (grep: 0 files); KELD-GUARD006 = NotAppProcess; KELD-IPC-007 = HelloAuth.

FACT (kel139 spec AC5; Linear KEL-143 Backlog and KEL-139 Done, fetched 2026-10-06): recovery keeps the same window and page; each affected pending call gets exactly one terminal outcome, with no claim about commit and no replay.
INFERENCE, decided on map (PANEL-D6, F02-EPIC, F02-T2): facade objects are host-minted (handle, generation) pairs with a mirror updated before user listeners run.
INFERENCE, decided on map (PANEL-D5, F02-T3): two-phase close via CloseRequested{window, generation, seq}; the host waits indefinitely while the owning generation is alive; no auto-close on timeout.
INFERENCE, decided on map (PANEL-D5, F02-T3): the host closes on its own only at generation revocation. Encoded as the default option.

INFERENCE, decided on map (F01-T3, F01-T2, PANEL-D5): two-phase host-owned quit, cancellable at before-quit, will-quit or any window veto; Cmd+Q via applicationShouldTerminate delayed reply; a successor receives Ready again and re-adopts.
INFERENCE, prototype: a retired generation's reconnect maps to KELD-IPC-007; WindowGeneration does not rotate on Bun recovery; destroy()/show()/close() on a dead object throw the same TypeError.
PROPOSED (PANEL-D19 contested): unhealthy-role signal and diagnostic shape; the model flags after one deadline period.
PROPOSED (PANEL-D23 contested, PANEL-P2 not run): quit sweep sequencing on AppKit; both all-at-once and serialized are selectable.
PROPOSED (F02-A3 open): the ready-to-show paint oracle on system webviews.
PROPOSED (F02-A2 refuter; F02-T3 says only 'idempotent'): repeated close attempts coalesce, so same-tick double close() emits close once.
PROPOSED (not specified on map): adoption contract shape (WindowAdopted snapshot before Ready, no listeners carried, ready-to-show not replayed).
PROPOSED (not specified on map): a close requested while no generation is alive, and the LastWindowClosed owed to the successor.
PROPOSED (not specified on map): a quit in flight at generation loss is cancelled; Cmd+Q with no live generation follows the close option.
PROPOSED (contradiction): win.id is host-minted in the model. F02-A1 proposes a facade-local counter that is never the host WindowId; F02-T2 requires 'id is host-minted'.
PROPOSED (not specified on map): how new BrowserWindow() returns a host-minted identity synchronously when the Bun kipc client cannot block (PANEL-D2); the model treats minting as atomic.

PROPOSED (prototype names): messages QuitBegin, QuitSweepComplete, QuitCancelled, QuitRequested, WindowAdopted, CloseVeto; placeholder codes KELD-IPC-GENERATION-RETIRED, KELD-IPC-CLOSE-SEQ, KELD-COMPAT-WEBPREFS (KELD-COMPAT-001..009 are already taken).
proto.caveats:
Findings the orchestrator should route:
1. Data-loss edge in decided text. PANEL-D5/F02-T3 "host closes on its own when the generation is revoked" destroys a window whose veto listener never ran. This contradicts the stated reason for refusing auto-close and KEL-143's same-window continuity. The keep-window alternative avoids it; neither is settled for the generation gap (F02-A2 refuter: "pick one in the registry spec").
2. Adoption hole. After recovery, adopted windows have no app listeners (they died with g1), so a later close proceeds without the app's save prompt. An unmodified Electron app that creates its window in a ready handler would also create a second window. F01-T2 says only "can re-adopt".
3. win.id contradiction between F02-A1 (facade-local counter) and F02-T2 (host-minted).
4. Synchronous constructor. No ticket says how new BrowserWindow() gets a host-minted identity when the Bun client cannot block (PANEL-D2).
5. Mechanism difference. Electron's Cmd+Q is a terminate: override, not applicationShouldTerminate. Keld's NSTerminateLater route parks the host run loop in a modal-panel mode while it waits; the effect on host kipc I/O sources during an indefinite wait is UNKNOWN and belongs in PANEL-P2.
6. Same-tick double close(). Whether Electron emits close once or per attempt is UNKNOWN; the model emits it once.

Not modelled: renderer beforeunload vetoes, app.exit(), quitAndInstall ordering, parent/modal windows, a throwing close listener, app.quit() called inside a close listener (the Zettlr pattern), JS re-entrancy during a modal dialog (PANEL-D22), the interim rule where the first new BrowserWindow() adopts the host-created primary window, and Windows/Linux hooks.

Verification limits: the logic and scenarios ran headlessly in Node; the page script ran against a stub DOM (all 32 buttons over three rounds, all three walkthroughs, both option selects; zero exceptions, zero silent successes). Headless Chrome rendered it at 1280px and 500px with no horizontal overflow after one CSS fix. Only the dark theme was seen (this machine's setting); the light theme and widths under 500px were not rendered. No real browser clicks were made.

Process: the only file left behind is the prototype. A temporary receipts directory under notes/ and a temporary screenshot directory were created and removed. Nothing was written to the Keld repo, GitHub or Linear.

judge.verdict:
PASS AFTER FIXES. In the model, a host-owned window registry reproduces the Electron v44.4.5 lifecycle named in the question, and windows survive a Bun crash and re-adoption, with one exception that follows the map text: a window with an unanswered close is closed by the host when its generation is revoked. This is a logic model, not OS evidence.

The original file passed its own 117 checks but had six real defects (five against pinned Electron source or docs, one against the Keld bounded-queue rule), all now fixed in place. After the fixes: 142/142 scripted expectations hold, 240,000 fuzzed actions across all four option combinations break no invariant, and all 38 walkthrough steps run through the page handlers against a stub document with no failed check.

Checklist:
- (a) Liftable logic: yes. The logic and scenario scripts run in a bare sandbox with no document, window, console or timers.
- (b) Walkthroughs: every scenario in the question now has a step that drives the module (see scenario_coverage).
- (c) Names and ordering: checked against pinned browser-window.md, base-window.md, app.md and the cited source files. The line numbers the prototype cites are correct.
- (c) Keld facts: KELD-GUARD006 and KELD-IPC-007 exist at b4b907c3 where cited. The Apple windowShouldClose and terminateLater texts were re-fetched and match.
- (d) Typed errors: illegal actions return TypeError "Object has been destroyed", registered KELD codes, or placeholder KELD codes marked unregistered. Moves with no real actor return PROTOTYPE-PRECONDITION, labelled as not a product error.
- (e) Open decisions: 15 rows are labelled PROPOSED.
- (f) Standalone: valid HTML, balanced tags, no external resources.

Linear was reachable in this session. KEL-143 is Backlog, unassigned, blocked by KEL-142/140/134/133/118/139; KEL-139 is Done (both fetched 2026-10-06), matching the prototype's FACT row.

Strongest remaining reason the prototype could be wrong: its oracle is the same reading of Electron source that shaped the design, not an Electron transcript (PANEL-P2 has not run). Each dispatch also runs host and Bun to quiescence, so the only interleavings it can explore are "Bun parked" and "same tick".
mismatches: FIXED, Electron source: destroy() on an already destroyed object threw TypeError. In v44.4.5 destroy() and isDestroyed() are installed by gin_helper Destroyable (destroyable.cc DestroyFunc returns early when IsDestroyed), so it is a silent no-op. base-window.md line 607 says 'most' members throw.
FIXED, Electron observable: win.destroy() followed by win.isDestroyed() in the same tick returned false. Electron's DestroyFunc clears the wrapper before returning, so it is true at once.

FIXED, Electron docs (app.md window-all-closed): a user close crossed with Cmd+Q while Bun was parked emitted window-all-closed in the middle of a quit (close, before-quit, closed, window-all-closed, will-quit, quit).

FIXED, Keld invariant (stale handle rejected, host is the authority): win.destroy() then win.show() in one tick made the host mark a destroyed window visible with no error. Nothing on the host checked the (WindowId, WindowGeneration) pair; only the facade fence did.
FIXED, Keld invariant (bounded queues, docs/architecture/02-ipc.md lines 248-256): renderer invokes in flight were unbounded. 50 invokes against a parked Bun gave 50 queued calls.

FIXED, ambiguous-outcome error: an invoke made while no generation is admitted was rejected with text saying 'the handler may or may not have committed'. It was never delivered, so its outcome is known.
FIXED, minor: win.on / removeAllListeners on a destroyed object threw TypeError. They are plain EventEmitter JavaScript and do not throw.

FIXED, labelling: the INFERENCE row claimed destroy() throws on a dead object. No row recorded that Keld emits close and closed after a host round trip, whereas Electron on macOS emits them inside win.close() and win.destroy() (source reading, no fixture run).
FIXED, coverage: no walkthrough showed window-all-closed waiting for the last of several windows, and none showed destroy() on its own (the only destroy step followed a vetoed close).

OPEN, not changed (map text encoded faithfully and already flagged by the prototype): the default option closes a window with an unanswered close when its generation is revoked (PANEL-D5, F02-T3 acceptance criterion 3). That contradicts 'Bun can crash without the window disappearing' and KEL-139 AC5 same-window-and-document recovery for exactly the draw.io pattern (close listener that always vetoes). The alternative 'keep-window' option is modelled and labelled PROPOSED; the map needs to pick one.

OPEN, labelled PROPOSED: the all-at-once quit sweep emits close(w2), close(w1), closed(w2), closed(w1). Whether Electron interleaves closed between the close events depends on whether WebContents::Close() is synchronous; unverified until PANEL-P2 runs.
OPEN, labelled PROPOSED: repeated close attempts coalesce into one close event while unanswered. The F02 refuter says Electron re-emits close per attempt.

OPEN, labelled PROPOSED: a successor generation receives ready again, so an unmodified app that creates its window in the ready handler would create a second window. The adoption contract is not specified on the map.

NOTE: the prototype cites F02-A1, F02-A2 and F01-A2. These are research-unit decision ids in swarm.json, not published tickets in publish_plan.json (only F02-A3 and F02-A6 are published for F02). The citations are accurate as research references.

NOTE: the model emits ready-to-show for visible windows too. That matches source (electron_api_web_contents.cc OnFirstNonEmptyLayout plus lib/browser/api/web-contents.ts lines 765-771 forward it regardless of visibility), while the doc text says 'while not being shown'. It stays PROPOSED under F02-A3.
judge.fixes_applied:
All edits are in the file and keep the three-script boundary (pure logic, DOM-free scenarios, page rendering).

Logic module:
1. winDestroy on a tombstoned object is now a silent no-op with zero kipc frames, not a TypeError.
2. winDestroy flips the facade tombstone inside the call, so isDestroyed() is true in the same tick. closed is still emitted exactly once, when the host's Destroyed arrives (new closedEmitted flag). A new invariant requires that a flipped tombstone always has closed emitted or queued.
3. New hostAdmitWindowCall checks every window command (show, hide, close) against the registry. A dead or forged (WindowId, WindowGeneration) returns placeholder typed error KELD-IPC-WINDOW-STALE (registered: false). A new hostile action rawWindowCall bypasses the facade fence to exercise it. A new invariant says a destroyed window is never visible.
4. The facade suppresses window-all-closed when a LastWindowClosed crosses a quit the generation has already begun.
5. New CALL_CREDIT = 4 (exported, labelled as an invented number). An invoke beyond the per-window window is not admitted: the sender suspends, the host queues nothing, and no error is raised. New invariants cover calls per window within the credit window and at most one queued host-to-Bun event of a kind per target.
6. KELD-IPC-GENERATION-RETIRED at admission now says "rejected before delivery ... Outcome known: no handler ran", with retry-safe fix text. The in-flight case keeps the ambiguous-outcome text.

judge.scenario_coverage:
Three walkthrough tabs, 38 steps, every one dispatching into the logic module and asserting the event order plus model invariants.

Happy path (11 steps):
- ready-to-show (painted while hidden), then show
- user close vetoed by preventDefault, window kept
- win.close() giving close, tombstone, closed, then window-all-closed and the default quit (before-quit, will-quit, quit)
- two windows: window-all-closed only after the last closed
- app.quit() with two windows: before-quit, per-window close, closed, will-quit, quit, and no window-all-closed
- Bun crash with the window still on screen, successor re-adopts the same (w1, wg1) with no ready-to-show replay, successor closes the adopted window

Tricky edges (17 steps):
- close while Bun is parked: waits, no auto-close after deadline periods, role flagged, second click coalesced, resume and veto
- destroy() after a vetoed close; destroy() alone (no close, closed once, isDestroyed() true in the same tick, second destroy() a no-op)
- a close crossing Cmd+Q while parked
- invoke flood stopped at the credit window
- close() twice in one tick
- app.quit() vetoed by one of two windows; the serialized-sweep alternative
- Cmd+Q cancelled at before-quit (applicationShouldTerminate later, then reply NO); Cmd+Q going through (reply YES, windowShouldClose never runs)
- will-quit vetoed, then quit again
- crash with an invoke in flight and an unanswered close under both policies; the successor after it

Illegal attempts (10 steps):
- getBounds, show and close after closed throw TypeError "Object has been destroyed"; isDestroyed() is the safe probe; destroy() on a dead object is a no-op
- nodeIntegration gives KELD-COMPAT-WEBPREFS
- a renderer window command gives KELD-GUARD006
- a forged CloseAllow gives KELD-IPC-CLOSE-SEQ
- a raw dead or forged window handle gives KELD-IPC-WINDOW-STALE
- a facade call while parked (not issuable) and no auto-close after three periods
- an invoke with no live generation (rejected before delivery) and a retired generation's HELLO (KELD-IPC-007)
- the successor reaching for a window destroyed before it existed

Not modelled, and labelled PROPOSED in the table: renderer beforeunload vetoes, app.exit(), quitAndInstall ordering, parent and modal windows, a throwing close listener, app.quit() inside a close listener, JavaScript re-entrancy during a modal dialog, primary-window adoption, and the fate of suspended senders at generation loss.

proto.question: Does host-mediated IPC (renderer -> Rust host -> Bun role over one kipc link) reproduce Electron v44.4.5 ipcMain/ipcRenderer semantics? Short answer from the model: yes for every decided semantic, with no contradiction between them. All 108 scripted steps across five walkthroughs produce the expected outcome, and each of the four ticket-named negative controls flips exactly its own invariant. Three behaviours the question treats as settled are not settled on the map and are encoded as PROPOSED: the sendSync blocking path (F04-A5), the grant evaluator and its matching grammar (F04-A1), and the worker-owned link (PANEL-P1). The model also shows that the worker-owned link alone only moves the stall point; it needs host credit windows to remove it.
proto.module_shape: One classic <script> block defining `KeldIpcBridge` (IIFE, plain-JSON state, no DOM/window/document/timers/Date/random/console; token-scanned clean). API: `init(overrides) -> state`; `step(state, action) -> { state, changes[{kind,text}], error|null, value }` (input state is never mutated; verified); `invariants(state) -> [{id,text,ok,detail}]` for grant, generation, bounded, order, endpoint, link; `describe(action) -> string` in Electron API / Keld terms; `DEFAULTS`; `SCENARIOS` (five walkthrough scripts with `expect` code and `has` substring per step, usable as fixtures). 26 action types: ipcRenderer.on/send/invoke/sendSync, renderer.openBunEndpoint, renderer.setBusy, ipcMain.on/handle/removeHandler, main.runTurn, main.openSecondLink, main.blockingCall, event.reply, event.senderFrame, event.setReturnValue, webContents.send, probe.parkMain, host.emitEvent, host.replyBlockingCall, clock.advance (chronological deadline processing on a logical clock), webview.navigate/hashChange/destroy, manifest.grant, migrate.run, config.set, mutation.set. Errors are objects `{code, allocated, label, message, fix, source, surfacedTo}`; `allocated:true` = code exists in Keld today (KELD-GUARD003, KELD-IPC-006), `false` = symbolic placeholder shown with a trailing `*`, `null` = Electron's own exception text or CANNOT-OCCUR. It also exports via `module.exports` when present, so it runs under node/bun unchanged. A second <script> is page glue only (reads inputs, calls step, renders).
scenarios: Happy path (17 steps): ipcMain.handle + ipcRenderer.invoke round trip with host-minted correlation; three ipcRenderer.send on one channel dispatched to ipcMain.on as seq 1,2,3; event.senderFrame.url host-minted; event.reply to the sender document; webContents.send to the current main frame of webview #1 only; hash change keeps the generation so a later event.reply still arrives; keld migrate writes enumerated grants.

Tricky edges (29 steps): handler throw gives the renderer Electron's message-only error while the typed code stays on the bun->host wire line and in diagnostics; navigation race where event.senderFrame becomes null, the late event.reply is dropped silently even though the new document listens on the same channel, and webContents.send follows the webview to generation 2; renderer credit window (four overlapping invokes accepted, fifth refused with a typed error, link invariant stays green, credit returns after a main turn); navigate with pending invokes (KELD-WV-011, reply rejected before dispatch); main->renderer bounded hold while the renderer is busy, fifth refused, ordered drain.

Illegal attempts (18 steps): ungranted channel -> KELD-GUARD003 with the manifest patch; popup webview principal with channels [] -> KELD-GUARD003; keld migrate asked for el:* -> refused; hand-written el:* -> refused; enumerated grant then admitted, then Electron's exact 'No handler registered' rejection; sendSync -> scaffold throw with fix-it to invoke; page asks for a Bun endpoint -> refused; second ipcMain.handle -> Electron's exact text; blocking main-side call on a main-owned socket -> refused; second kipc link -> refused; 2 MiB inline payload -> refused; webContents.send to a destroyed webview -> 'Object has been destroyed'; send from a destroyed webview and reply to an unknown event -> CANNOT-OCCUR.

sendSync (22 steps): decided scaffold throw first; then an explicit HYPOTHETICAL switch (experiment F04-A5 assumed passed) exercising the blocking CALL: dev warning, renderer blocked (other renderer actions cannot occur), reply sent at the moment event.returnValue is assigned, 2000 ms deadline -> typed deadline error with the late returnValue dropped, third call within a second -> typed rate-limit error, no-listener case logging Electron's 'without listeners' warning and ending by deadline.

Parked Bun main (23 steps, one mid-script reset): arm A main-owned socket: product refuses the blocking call; forced park probe; host REPLY cannot reach the parked reader; host events fill the socket and the writer stalls at exactly 8,192 bytes; an unrelated renderer invoke is refused; +5 s -> KELD-IPC-006, link closed. Reset to arm B worker-owned single link: blocking call admitted, 12 KiB of events buffered in order in the ring with no stall, renderer invoke accepted, REPLY wakes main via the worker, buffered frames replay in arrival order.

judge.fixes_applied: All edits are in the one HTML file; the pure-module boundary is kept (code with strings and comments stripped has no DOM or global references, and the module ran every scenario without touching a trap `document`). Logic module: (1) deliver() holds main-to-renderer events while the renderer is blocked in sendSync, bounded by the same window; new drainHeld() releases them on returnValue, deadline, link loss or end of long task. (2) Credit leak closed: a sync CALL with a closed reply slot returns its credit when Bun consumes it, and one already consumed returns it when its document navigates or is destroyed; new 'credit' invariant (every held credit belongs to an in-flight frame or the live blocked sendSync). (3) New mainLink() guard: webContents.send, event.reply, returnValue replies and event-loop dispatch fail with KELD-IPC-006 once the link is closed. (4) event.senderFrame.url now reads the live host-registry URL. (5) KELD-IPC-LINK-STALLED* relabelled PROPOSED with corrected source text. (6) Park-timeout text is transport-specific and states that nothing is closed or dismissed on timeout and that a deadline on a user-paced modal is PROPOSED. (7) Credit and payload error sources name KELD-WV-011 as the default code to reuse. (8) A refused ipcRenderer.send emits a host diagnostic plus an explicit 'ELECTRON DIVERGENCE (PROPOSED, open)' callout, with its surfacing marked OPEN. (9) Link loss settles a blocked sendSync with an error; navigation clears the busy flag. proto.question:
Does the keld migrate analyzer state model (scan → inventory per Electron member → classify against the compat matrix → native-module qualification → security blockers listed separately → authority profile printed → five files only after --write → counts labelled "static estimate, not a compatibility score" → KEL-74 claim line only against a committed denominator) ever let the report say more than the evidence supports?

Answer from the prototype: no, within the model. Run headlessly under Node, all three walkthroughs matched their expectations (15 + 27 + 36 = 78 steps, 0 mismatches), the eight honesty invariants held on every rendered report, and each of nine report mutations was caught by at least one invariant. Not checked in a real browser (see caveats).

What the model showed that the map should know:
1. Honest today means nearly all "tracked". The draw.io-like inventory (22 members, 68 resolved call sites) classifies as 2 call sites behavior-match (app.whenReady), 5 documented divergence (app.quit), 60 tracked, 1 unclassified (electron-updater setFeedURL has no matrix row). Zettlr-like: 24 members, 440 sites, 429 tracked.
2. A claim line needs an accepted legacy forfeit. The live evidence profile enum has four variants and none is `unverified`, so no KEL-74 record can exist for an app left at the default profile (live KELD-COMPAT-005). The model makes this an explicit precondition; the map does not state it.
3. Decided-but-unlanded dispositions must not move a row. webRequest "recorded no-op" (PANEL-D17) and setFeedURL "recorded no-op" (PANEL-D14) stay tracked/unclassified until a conformance entry lands; the webRequest one additionally refuses to land before the host containment proof.
4. Evidence does not generalize: better-sqlite3 13.0.3 reads qualified at win32-x64 and unqualified at darwin-arm64 from the same ledger; a denominator for draw.io yields no claim line for Zettlr; a modified tree withdraws the claim.
scenarios: Happy path (draw.io-like, 15 steps): scan → inventory → classify → natives → security blockers → profile → report (no percentage, no files, explicit no-claim reason) → accept legacy forfeit → authorize --write → re-run withdrawn stages → generate five files (15 enumerated el:<channel> grants, 2 literal origins, 1 app-scoped fs root; dynamic openExternal and dispatcher channels not seeded) → denominators committed → corpus id documented → smoke records attached → three claim lines: 1/1 install, 1/1 activation, 3/4 primary_workflow (close-with-unsaved-prompt unknown, it runs dialog.showMessageBoxSync). Static counts do not move.

Tricky edges (27 steps): Zettlr-like — forge.config.js and webpack configs listed and never evaluated; sandbox:false x2 is ignored with a diagnostic and the profile stays unverified; nodehun 3.0.2 and fsevents unqualified, chokidar 5 not a native addon; three shell:true spawns are never mapped; six sendSync sites are a compatibility blocker; generic window.ipc dispatcher makes channels unenumerable; committing a denominator still yields no claim line because Zettlr is not a corpus member.

Tricky edges, native evidence: a full KEL-215-shaped nodehun row at darwin-arm64 qualifies it for exactly that tuple; switching target to win32-x64 makes it unqualified again. Synthetic legacy app: better-sqlite3 13.0.3 qualified at win32-x64 (live row) and unqualified at darwin-arm64; remote and sharedTexture are never; computed member access is unclassified; nodeIntegration:true is a never.

Tricky edges, draw.io webRequest: landing the recorded no-op before the containment proof fails (KELD-COMPAT-109, proposed code); after the proof it lands and 2 call sites move from tracked to documented divergence, nothing becomes behavior-match; claim lines appear after legacy + --write + generation + records, then are withdrawn when the scanned tree is modified.

Illegal attempts (36 steps, 21 typed errors): classify before scan; generate without --write; generate from a stale analysis; evaluate forge.config.js; print a percentage; force a claim line with no denominator; commit an empty denominator (live KELD-COMPAT-008); attach records under unverified (live KELD-COMPAT-005); mark a cell or a native module passing on import success; seed el:*, $HOME/**, https://** or a channel not in source; select strict; infer legacy from sandbox:false; write legacy without acknowledging the forfeit; translate setFeedURL into a feed; carry nodeIntegration:true; map a shell:true spawn; land sendSync as supported.

Negative controls (9 mutations of a rendered report copy, each caught): inject the arch 04 sample line 'compat score: 91%'; drop the static-estimate label; hide unclassified/never rows; forge a claim line from static counts; qualify native modules by package name; print legacy without a forfeit; print strict; seed el:*; fold the security section away.

Free play: 51 buttons in five groups (analyzer stages, user choices, simulated world inputs, refused attempts, negative controls), always enabled; exercised against three starting states with no throw and no unknown action.

proto.module_shape:
Three script blocks in one self-contained HTML file (no framework, no server, no external resources; 0 external src/href).

1. `<script id="migrate-data">` — `KELD_MIGRATE_DATA`, pure data: matrix slice (30 members with status, tier, family, Linear owners), never-list, landable dispositions, the two live KEL-215 rows, the electron-apps-v0 corpus sketch, and three scan fixtures (drawio-like, zettlr-like, synthetic-legacy). In the real analyzer these are inputs.

2. `<script id="migrate-logic">` — `createMigrateModel(DATA)`, the liftable module. Verified to have no document/window/Date/random/timer/console references outside string literals and comments. Returns `{ PHASES, LABEL, GLYPH, MUTATIONS, initialState, reduce, checkInvariants, factsOf, claimStatus }`.
   - `reduce(state, action) -> { state, changes[], error|null }`; a reducer over an explicit phase machine `idle → scanned → inventoried → classified → natives → security → profiled → reported`. It clones, never mutates the previous state, and on error returns the previous state object unchanged.
   - Errors are `{ code, live, message, cause, fix, docs }` (the live KeldErrorObject shape plus a `live` flag separating codes that exist on origin/main from proposed numbers).
   - `invalidate(state, toPhase)` steps the phase back and clears derived outputs whenever an input changes, so a stale report cannot be shown.
   - Pure builders per stage: `buildInventory`, `classifyMember` / `buildClassification`, `qualify`, `buildBlockers`, `buildProfilePrint`, `claimStatus`, `derivedGrants` / `validateGrant` / `buildGenerated`, `buildReport`.
   - `checkInvariants(report, facts)` is the oracle (I1 no percentage, I2 label present, I3 conservation of members and call sites, I4 claim preconditions and shape, I5 native qualification, I6 profile, I7 write authorization and no wildcard channel, I8 security section separate). `factsOf(state)` derives ground truth from state, never from the report.
   - Action types: reset, scan, inventory, classify, qualifyNatives, listSecurityBlockers, printAuthorityProfile, renderReport, analyze, acceptLegacyForfeit, authorizeWrite, generateFiles, setTarget, recordContainmentProof, landConformance, addNativeEvidence, commitDenominator, documentCorpusId, attachCellEvidence, modifyWorkingTree, executeAppConfig, printPercentage, emitClaimLine, seedGrant, requestStrict, inferLegacyFromSandbox, markQualifiedFromImport, translateSetFeedURL, carryNodeIntegration, mapShellTrueSpawn, probeMutation.

3. `<script id="page">` — rendering and wiring only: intro, three tabbed walkthroughs (reset / next step / run all, with per-step expectation checks), 51 free-play buttons, the state panel re-rendered after every action with "what just changed" callouts or the typed error, and the 38-row "Assumptions and decisions encoded" table.

judge.verdict:
PASS AFTER FIXES. The state model answers the question honestly once 14 mismatches were corrected in place; the pure-module boundary is intact. Before the fixes it could overstate in two ways: "qualified" ignored artifact identity, and legacy smoke records could attach to files generated without the legacy key.

Linear availability (the relayed user request): Linear is AVAILABLE in this session. Four read-only get_issue calls succeeded on 2026-10-06: KEL-74 Done, KEL-215 Done, KEL-78 In Progress, KEL-237 In Progress. All four match the statuses the prototype cites. No Linear writes were made. The mempalace MCP server failed to connect (executable not found); nothing here depended on it.

Strongest plausible reason the prototype was wrong: its honesty oracle shared the implementation's mistakes. factsOf() took "qualified" from qualify() and claim eligibility from claimStatus(), the same functions that produced the report. A bug in either would pass the checker. It now recomputes both from raw world inputs. Four producer mutations confirm the independence: qualify ignoring the artifact gives I5; the claim ignoring a dirty tree gives I4; unknown counted as pass gives I4; unclassified members dropped gives I3. The unmodified module is clean on the same flows.

Checks:
(a) Liftable: yes. The data and logic blocks run in a bare vm context with no document, window, clock or randomness. reduce() never mutates its input and returns the prior state unchanged on error.
(b) Walkthroughs drive the module: happy 15/15, edges 29/29, illegal 42/42 steps match expectations when run headlessly through the page's own click handler. A separate assertion script checks concrete outcomes rather than only ok/error.
(c) Electron v44.4.5 receipts, fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com on 2026-10-06, all hold:
- web-request.md: "Only the last attached `listener` will be used."
- structures/web-preferences.md: sandbox "Default is `true` since Electron 20. The sandbox will automatically be disabled when `nodeIntegration` is set to `true`"; contextIsolation "Defaults to `true`".
- breaking-changes.md: "Removed: `remote` module" sits under "Breaking API Changes (14.0)".
- tutorial/security.md item 15 covers shell.openExternal with untrusted content.
Member names match the matrix entities. The Keld-side mismatches found against origin/main are listed below and fixed.
(d) Illegal actions return a typed error {code, message, cause, fix, docs}; 24 error paths were asserted by code.
(e) Open decisions are labelled PROPOSED: X02-A1, X04-D4, X03-A5, F01-A4, X04-D3, the profile key, error numbering and file contents.
(f) Valid standalone HTML: balanced tags, doctype present, no src/href/@import/fetch, 121 KB.

All nine stages in the question are driven through the module by guided walkthroughs.

Happy path (15 steps, draw.io-like): scan, inventory, classify, natives, security blockers, profile, report, accept legacy, authorize --write, generate, commit denominator, document corpus id, attach smoke records, then three KEL-74 claim lines (1/1 install, 1/1 activation, 3/4 primary_workflow).

Tricky edges (29 steps):
- Zettlr-like: sandbox:false x2 ignored, nodehun and fsevents unqualified, three shell:true spawns never mapped, six sendSync sites, generic dispatcher, no claim despite a committed denominator.
- Evidence does not generalize: artifact mismatch, then match, then target switch to win32.
- Synthetic legacy app: remote, sharedTexture, computed member access, nodeIntegration:true.
- draw.io-like again: webRequest gated on the containment proof, then claim lines withdrawn when the tree is modified.

proto.question: Does the compatibility-matrix cell state machine encode the maturity ladder honestly? Answer from the prototype: yes for the top three rungs, waivers and percentages, which are backed by X01-EPIC and the live KEL-74 scorer. It only holds together with four rules the map does not contain (see caveats): what closes a P1, that a regression cannot be relabelled as a ▲, that a ▲ cell cannot also hold a rung, and that every BEHAVIOR_MATCH cell (not only observed-only ones) is recorded `unknown` rather than `pass`. All 67 walkthrough steps (19 happy, 23 edges, 25 illegal) produced their expected result when the logic block ran under Node with no DOM, and refusals left state unchanged.
proto.module_shape: Single IIFE `KeldCompatCell` in `<script id="logic">`, ES5-style, no DOM or global access (it ran under Node with no `window`/`document` defined; the only textual match left is the doc file name `browser-window.md`). State is plain JSON: `{ asOf, seq, cells{id -> {rung, mark: none|divergence|never, divergence, never, waiver, facts{memberExists, typedError, entry, ownedTest, implemented, golden, normalisers, lanes{macos,windows,linux}, laneGap, authorityProfile, negativeControl, corpus}}}, denominator, committedProductCorpora, tooling, p1[] }`. Public surface: `initialState()`, `dispatch(state, action) -> { ok, state, changes[], error{code, allocation: live|proposed, message, fix, source}, action }` (never mutates its input; a refusal returns the previous state), `gates(cell, state)` (15 gates tagged by rung, cumulative), `supported(cell, state)`, `ledger(cell, lane)` (KEL-74 result pass|fail|unknown|waived|null), `score(state, lane)` (mirrors `evidence.rs` `score()`), `observe(cell)`, `runStep(state, step)`, plus `CATALOGUE` (6 cells) and `WALKTHROUGHS` (pure data, usable as test vectors). 23 action types: LAND_SCAFFOLD, LAND_CONFORMANCE_ENTRY, IMPLEMENT, RUN_OWNED_TEST, PROVE_NEGATIVE_CONTROL, RECORD_GOLDEN, DECLARE_NORMALISERS, REPLAY, RECORD_LANE_GAP, RUN_CORPUS, CLAIM_RUNG, ACCEPT_DIVERGENCE, RETIRE_DIVERGENCE, MARK_NEVER, REGRESS, WAIVE, DROP_WAIVER, ACCEPT_LOWERED_MANIFEST, CALL_FROM_APP, TOOLING_LANDS, ADVANCE_CLOCK, COMMIT_DENOMINATOR, DOCUMENT_PRODUCT_CORPUS, PUBLISH_PERCENT. Design choice: the rung is a manifest claim checked against evidence, so adding evidence never promotes by itself, and losing evidence under a claimed rung demotes to the highest rung still supported and appends a P1. The page script only renders and wires 51 always-enabled buttons and three tabbed walkthroughs.
scenarios: Happy path (19 steps, `app.quit()` ordering before-quit -> window close -> will-quit): scaffold, claim L0, red conformance entry citing app.md, implement, claim L1, golden under Electron 44.4.5, normalisers, macOS replay, claim BEHAVIOR_MATCH (record stays `unknown`), owned test green, negative control proven, Windows and Linux replays, claim CONFORMANCE_PASS (record becomes `pass`), corpus run refused today with live KELD-CLI-045, hypothetical tooling-live step, draw.io corpus run with legacy profile printed, claim CORPUS_VERIFIED, one-cell showcase denominator, publish `1/1 of showcase corpus ...@digest (primary_workflow)`.

Tricky edges (23 steps): negative control goes dead -> demotion CONFORMANCE_PASS to BEHAVIOR_MATCH plus P1, closed by re-proving and re-claiming; Linux lane starts to differ -> second P1, and relabelling that lane as a ▲ gap is refused; observed-only `ready-to-show` vs `did-finish-load` cell reaches BEHAVIOR_MATCH and is refused above it; permission-handler divergence refused as a quirks flag (host constraint), accepted as scoreboard ▲ with record `fail` + intentional_divergence, then refused a rung claim; `dialog.showMessageBoxSync()` blocked at SCAFFOLDED by open PANEL-P1, waived for 14 days; four-cell denominator gives no percentage because one cell is `unknown`; clock +30 days makes `score()` fail closed with live KELD-COMPAT-006; product denominator publishes nothing until the corpus id is documented, then `1/2 ... (50%)`.

Illegal attempts (25 steps, each returns a typed error and leaves state unchanged): claim CORPUS_VERIFIED on an untouched cell; silent no-op scaffold; implement before the conformance entry; golden re-recorded from the Keld arm; normaliser that redacts all args; replay with no golden; replay labelled `strict_bun`; replay labelled `unverified` (live KELD-COMPAT-005); waiver with no owner, impossible date, past expiry, or on a passing cell (all live KELD-COMPAT-006); hand-port corpus evidence; corpus run while `keld migrate` is reserved (live KELD-CLI-045); corpus run on panel `product` with no committed id; quirks flag that widens authority; ✘ never with no never-list source or no fix-it; rung claim and waiver on a ✘ never cell; percentage with no denominator; empty and duplicate-cell denominators (live KELD-COMPAT-008); acknowledging a P1 that does not exist.

Free play: 51 always-enabled buttons in six groups (evidence, manifest claims and marks, regressions, waivers and clock, scoreboard, shortcuts the real system refuses), acting on any of six cells: `app.quit()` order, `nativeTheme` 'updated', `ready-to-show` order (observed-only), `session.setPermissionRequestHandler` with no handler (▲ candidate), `dialog.showMessageBoxSync()` (blocked by PANEL-P1), `session.loadExtension()` (✘ never candidate). A stub-DOM run pressed every button on every cell with no exception and no `undefined` in the output.
decisions_encoded: FACT - Top three rungs and their gates (BEHAVIOR_MATCH, CONFORMANCE_PASS, CORPUS_VERIFIED) as published in X01-EPIC 'Maturity ladder (this is the ladder every family uses)'. The X01-T1 spec that will own them is not written or approved.

PROPOSED - The six status names as a contract: UNSUPPORTED/SCAFFOLDED/PARTIAL appear only as 'Suggested status values' in the untracked reference doc section 25 and in scratchpad compat-matrix.tsv (2,088 UNSUPPORTED, 33 NEVER, 3 BEHAVIOR_MATCH, 2 BEHAVIOR_MATCH ▲, 1 SCAFFOLDED, 1 PARTIAL); no spec or code owns them.

INFERENCE - SCAFFOLDED = L0 (member exists, typed KELD-COMPAT throw, never a silent no-op) and PARTIAL = L1 (works on the macOS corpus path). The L0/L1 texts are fact in the F01/F05/F06 epics; the name mapping is stated nowhere.
FACT - Conformance entry citing the pinned doc sentence lands before implementation (root AGENTS.md, crates/keld-compat/AGENTS.md).
FACT - The pinned doc sentence is the oracle and the golden is evidence-of-record; goldens come only from the pinned Electron arm (X01-EPIC scope and never list).
PROPOSED - Normaliser set (pid, window id, paths, Error.stack) and the rule rejecting an over-broad normaliser: X01-A5 is open on the map.
FACT - Observed-only cells cap at BEHAVIOR_MATCH and are recorded `unknown` (X01-EPIC scope, X01-T1 acceptance criterion 3).
INFERENCE - A doc-cited cell at BEHAVIOR_MATCH is also `unknown` until its Keld-owned test and negative control hold; the refuters say this only for observed-only cells.

PROPOSED - The rung is a claimed field of the manifest cell while the KEL-74 verdict set stays pass|fail|unknown|waived (verdict set is live fact; rung placement is a refuter correction not yet in any spec).
INFERENCE - 'All three OS lanes or explicit ▲' read as: each lane without a pass needs an explicit ▲ gap with a reason and at least one lane really passes; a gap lane reports `fail` on that lane.

FACT - CORPUS_VERIFIED is unreachable today: `keld migrate` is reserved verb KELD-CLI-045 (crates/keld-cli/src/verb.rs) and `keld dev --headless --smoke` is not live. The 'tooling goes live' action is a labelled hypothetical.
INFERENCE - A corpus run asking for panel `product` is refused until the corpus id is committed. Live code is looser: product rows may exist and simply publish no percentage.
FACT - Only `legacy_sandbox_off` is an honest authority profile today; `strict_bun` is refused and `unverified` is not in the KEL-74 closed set (kel78 spec, evidence.rs parse_authority, PANEL-D12).

INFERENCE - Losing a gate under a claimed rung demotes to the highest supported rung and raises a P1. 'A compat regression is a P1' is fact (arch 04 section 6, keld-compat AGENTS.md); per-cell automatic demotion is this prototype's mechanism.
PROPOSED - A P1 closes when the lost rung is re-claimed on restored evidence, or the manifest is lowered by a reviewed decision with owner and reason. Nothing on the map says what closes one.
PROPOSED - A waiver, a ▲ relabel or a ✘ mark never closes a P1, and a lane with an open regression cannot be relabelled as a ▲ gap.

FACT - ▲ is recorded as `fail` with `intentional_divergence` and never counted in `passed` (live cell app.quit.return-contract in crates/keld-compat/fixtures/lifecycle-corpus; report shows 'oracle matches 2/3, intentional divergence 1').

FACT - ▲ routing: host/kipc constraints go to the scoreboard, per-app choices may be a keld.compat.ts quirks flag, a quirk never widens authority, never prose-only (PANEL-D9, PANEL-D10 resolved; compat-scoreboard.md).
INFERENCE - Accepting a ▲ needs a doc-cited oracle, a green Keld-owned test of the divergent behaviour and a proven negative control (generalised from PANEL-D9 and the live cell's fields).
PROPOSED - A cell marked ▲ cannot also claim a higher rung; split the member into one cell per observable.
FACT - A missing permission handler is a deny, recorded ▲ against Electron auto-approve (F05-EPIC design facts; F05-D2 survived both refuters).
FACT - ✘ never needs a published never-list source and a fix-it and reports `fail` (PANEL-D9, PANEL-D10, per-epic never lists).
INFERENCE - ✘ never is terminal inside the state machine: only its L0 typed stub and observation are accepted; reopening needs a new approved spec.

FACT - Waivers need owner, reason and expiry; an expired waiver makes `score()` return KELD-COMPAT-006 for the whole board; a waiver cannot pair with `pass`; a waived cell counts in N, not in `passed`, and blocks `complete` (evidence.rs, compat-scoreboard.md rule 5). The live check is `expires_on < as_of`, so a waiver expiring today is still valid.

FACT - A percentage exists only against a committed denominator, is omitted with any missing or `unknown` cell or for panel `product` without a documented committed id (that list is empty today), and the only claim shape is `{passed}/{N} of {panel} corpus {id}@{digest} ({kind})` (evidence.rs score(), compat-scoreboard.md rules 1-4).
FACT - `dialog.showMessageBoxSync()` stays SCAFFOLDED until the S0 link-drain gate reports (F06-EPIC, PANEL-D3/D4 resolved, PANEL-P1 open); the prototype does not model the gate's outcome.
PROPOSED - Error codes KELD-COMPAT-L01..L19 are placeholders and not allocated. Live codes quoted with their real fix text: KELD-COMPAT-005, -006, -008 and KELD-CLI-045.
PROPOSED - Demo data: corpus id `electron-44.4.5-cell-demo-v1`, kind `primary_workflow` (mirrors the live electron-lifecycle-v0 corpus), and a labelled non-sha256 digest stand-in.

FINDINGS THAT CONTRADICT OR EXTEND THE MAP:
1. Doc receipt contradicts "docs silent". X01 research and both refuters say Electron's docs never order `ready-to-show` against `did-finish-load`. Pinned browser-window.md v44.4.5 lines 50-52 say: "This event is usually emitted after the `did-finish-load` event, but for pages with many remote resources, it may be emitted before the `did-finish-load` event." The cell is still observed-only, but for a stronger reason: the docs state both orders occur, so a recorded golden showing one order must never become a conformance assertion.
2. The matrix and the ledger disagree about ▲. compat-matrix.tsv prints `app.quit` as `BEHAVIOR_MATCH ▲ (Promise<void>)`; the live KEL-237 corpus records the same contract as a `fail` cell with `intentional_divergence`. The prototype follows the live ledger and refuses a rung claim on a ▲ cell.
3. The five BEHAVIOR_MATCH rows in compat-matrix.tsv cannot meet the X01 gate as written: no Electron 44.4.5 golden exists (X01-T2 is unbuilt; the live corpus is doc-cited tests pinned to 44.3.0, not transcripts). Under this state machine they would sit at PARTIAL, or the gate wording needs a clause for doc-cited tests that pre-date the recorder.
